articles.title: How Kiefer Sherwood Shows He’s Exactly What Sharks Needed
articles.summary: On one play Saturday night, Kiefer Sherwood showed he’s everything the San Jose Sharks needed. Sherwood has been a bit of an NHL journeyman. He started his c...
articles.body:
On one play Saturday night, Kiefer Sherwood showed he's everything the San Jose Sharks needed.

Sherwood has been a bit of an NHL journeyman. He started his career with the Anaheim Ducks, and has since played for the Colorado Avalanche, Nashville Predators and Vancouver Canucks.

The Sharks traded for him before the 2026 NHL trade deadline, though, and then made it a point to sign him to a contract extension.

Clearly, San Jose believed Sherwood was a good fit for their roster, and he's proving that very true.

On Saturday night, Sherwood made a play that was so much an epitome of who he is.

It's also exactly what the Sharks need him to do.

Sherwood put pressure on, stole the puck, and then slotted it home for a goal.

And as he skated away to celebrate, he hit a Kings player out of the way.

Defense, offense and physicality — all in one.

Think about what this Sharks team is — they're young talent hoping to rise up the NHL ranks, led by Macklin Celebrini, the best young player on the planet.

A team like that doesn't just need more production. A team like that needs a presence, someone who has seen it all, and someone who doesn't mind doing the dirty work.

Sherwood embraces physicality. He loves to set the tone. He knows what it takes to win NHL games.

That's an ideal player for the Sharks to have, and he's not really past his prime, either. He's arrived in San Jose at just the right time.

Sherwood entered the NHL as an undrafted player after playing his college hockey at Miami (Ohio).

His first two seasons were with the Ducks. He then had two with the Avs and two with the Predators.

Then it was a season-and-a-half with the Canucks before his trade with the Sharks.

This could be his longest tenure with San Jose, if he can prove to continue being this valuable.

Sherwood had his best NHL season in 2024-25 with the Canucks — he had 19 goals and 21 assists to go with an absurd 462 hits. He then had 339 hits and 36 points combined last season between Vancouver and San Jose.

Through two games this season, he already has 13 hits to go with that goal — and it doesn't count the post-goal hit, either.

Sherwood is exactly who he is, and it's exactly who the Sharks need.

articles.title: Why Joe Burrow's 'throw it more' mindset could be a problem for Bengals
articles.summary: Breaking down Joe Burrow's post-game comments about why he thinks the Bengals should be throwing the ball more
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have now lost two games in a row with the ball in their star quarterback's hands.

Joe Burrow , Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and Cincinnati's offense haven't been able to deliver at the moments they've needed it most, and because of that, Cincinnati has lost any head start it had in the division when it began the season 2-0.

It's still early, and no one should be panicking .

Photos: Bengals vs. Jaguars on Sunday October 4

But the fact that an offense with an elite quarterback, two of the NFL's best wide receivers and an offensive-minded head coach haven't won either game when they had their chances, poses a cause for concern. That includes the Oct. 4 loss to Jacksonville 22-17 at Paycor Stadium.

"You've got to execute in those moments," Burrow said. "Each play is its own story. You've got to try your best to execute as well as you can in the context of that story."

The Bengals returned all 11 starters on offense this season, the same offensive coordinator and head coach. Because of that, there was going to be no room for excuses on offense.

Through four games, the Bengals rank 14th in points (24.3), 31st in rushing offense (74.3 yards per game) and fourth in passing yards per game (277.5).

One of the areas the Bengals hoped to be better in this season was the run game. Cincinnati rushed for 23 yards against the Jaguars .

"We weren't good in the run game today; 23 yards was a reflection of how our run game was today," running back Chase Brown said.

To put the Bengals' run game woes in perspective, in the Bengals' most recent two losses, they've combined for 106 yards on the ground. Jacksonville rushed for 111 yards in their win over the Bengals in Week 4.

Burrow attempted 54 passes against Jacksonville, and the Bengals were still held to just 17 points. It begs the question: Are the Bengals becoming too dependent on Burrow throwing the ball and do they need a more balanced attack?

Not according to Burrow. But statistics suggest otherwise. The Bengals are 1-5 when Burrow attempts 50 or more passes.

Burrow said he thinks the Bengals should be throwing the ball even more. Here's why.

"Because I know we're great at it. Because I know that's what I do best and we're pass-protecting really well right now," he said. "Obviously, we'd like to get more out of the run game, but I know we'll make it work."The Bengals return their explosive running back in Brown who's begging for a monster year as he's in the final year of his rookie contract and wants to earn a second contract.

They return all of the same offensive linemen and the same run-game coordinators. So, why can't the Bengals run the ball more effectively?

No one will say. And Taylor refuses to call run plays for the sake of it. He believes the best chance for his team to win is with the ball in Burrow's hands more times than not.

And that's why when those instances occur, Burrow and Taylor must make the most of them or their way will be called into question.

The hope within the Bengals' locker room is that improvement is coming soon in the run game. Brown said they are "close" to hitting some big runs.

Cincinnati started off particularly slowly in this area last season. The Bengals didn't rush for more than 100 yards in their first six games of the 2025 season.

Taylor and his staff made a valiant effort to change things as the season went in hopes they could find more in the run game and had some success in doing so.

The Bengals rushed for 100 yards in their last four games of the 2025 season and nine of their last 11. They showed it can be done with these players.

There's reason to believe it can be done this season. But time is ticking, and as Burrow said, they need to find more "ways to score more points."

articles.title: Bills’ CJ Gardner-Johnson shades ‘practice squad player’ Efton Chism III despite insane game-winning TD catch
articles.summary: In one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 NFL season so far, the New England Patriots improved their record to 2-2 with a stunning road victory over the di...
articles.body:
In one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 NFL season so far, the New England Patriots improved their record to 2-2 with a stunning road victory over the division-rival Buffalo Bills . The upset was sealed by a breathtaking one-handed touchdown catch, labeled the Catch of the Year, made by unheralded wide receiver Efton Chism III . This remarkable play came from a stellar pass delivered by quarterback Drake Maye and ultimately helped secure the win after Bills star Josh Allen threw a late interception.

While New England celebrated this much-needed bounce-back victory, following a tough outing against Jacksonville, the mood in the losing locker room quickly turned tense. Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson expressed his frustration about the loss in a quote shared on X by ClutchPoints, aimed at the game's hero.

When discussing why Buffalo stumbled at home, Gardner-Johnson did not hold back. He stated, "An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won't hear from [Efton Chism III] again… respectfully. A practice squad player made a helluva play."

This dismissive comment has added significant bulletin-board material for the AFC East rivalry, demonstrating that the animosity between these two franchises remains as strong as ever. While Chism's jaw-dropping catch will be featured in highlight reels for weeks, Gardner-Johnson's remarks ensure that the rematch later this season will be filled with tension and competitive spirit.

articles.title: ‘I could see the real love’: 2028 4-star OL Georgia Tech wins recruitment of Sam Walker
articles.summary: Georgia Tech has won a major recruiting battle close to home. Sam Walker has committed to the Yellow Jackets over Clemson, Georgia and South Carolina. Clemso...
articles.body:
Georgia Tech has won an important recruiting battle close to home. Sam Walker has committed to the Yellow Jackets, choosing Georgia Tech over Clemson , Georgia and South Carolina . Clemson had previously positioned itself near the top of Walker's recruitment, while the Gamecocks remained heavily involved and Georgia made a push in recent months.

In the end, the four-star offensive lineman out of Carrollton (Ga.) Central decided to stay home.

"I would definitely say the relationship played a big role in my commitment," Walker told Rivals. "It's there. I can feel it. And then the school piece — it's a very good school. Say football doesn't work out, I still have business and stuff like that I can do. What Georgia Tech is, is for me."

Georgia Tech has been a consistent presence throughout Walker's recruitment. He has visited almost half a dozen times, including a trip earlier this season for the Yellow Jackets' game against Colorado.

But it was what happened away from campus Friday night that helped Walker become certain Georgia Tech was where he wanted to be. Members of the Yellow Jackets' staff made the trip to watch Walker play, reinforcing the relationships that had already put Georgia Tech in a strong position.

"They came to watch me play and I could see the real love. With me, him, Coach Mo, Keith — just all of us. I could just feel the love between all of us. The love we have is real."

Walker had been seriously considering Georgia Tech well before Friday. Seeing the staff show up for him helped close the deal.

"I've been thinking about them for a while, but I think Friday really did it," Walker said. "It just showed how much they make me feel like a priority."

That feeling ultimately helped Georgia Tech beat out a strong group of regional programs. Clemson had been one of Walker's top schools, South Carolina remained involved and Georgia had increased its pursuit in recent months.

Georgia Tech never stopped making Walker feel wanted. Relationships were only part of the equation.

Walker also placed significant value on what a Georgia Tech degree could provide beyond football. The combination of playing close to home and receiving an education from Georgia Tech became increasingly difficult to turn down.

Brent Key also provided Georgia Tech with another significant advantage. Key played offensive line for the Yellow Jackets before eventually returning to lead his alma mater. For Walker, the opportunity to play for a head coach who understands the position and places significant value on the offensive line resonated.

"Coach Tor (Brandon Torrey), Coach Mo (Allen Mogridge), all of them have talked to me about him being an offensive lineman," Walker said. "The offensive linemen that go there are very important to him. I really took that in. That was another reason I chose Tech."

By the end of Friday night, Walker knew. Georgia Tech had already built the relationships. Walker had already spent plenty of time on campus. He knew the academic opportunity, understood the program and had developed trust with the people recruiting him.

The staff showing up to watch him play provided the final push.

"I've always been thinking about them," Walker said. "But Friday, I think Friday really did it. For real, for real. It was a different feeling. I knew."

articles.title: Rookie Jacob Rodriguez makes plays for Dolphins vs. Vikings
articles.summary: Jacob Rodriguez, Chris Johnson and Kadyn Proctor are top Dolphins rookies. Here's the report card vs.Vikings
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS ― The Miami Dolphins played at the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 4, with rine rookies dressed to play.

Unfortunately, rookie receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle) was unable to go.

The Dolphins kept it closer than the experts expected for most the contest, but lost to the Vikings , 15-10.

Here is a rookie report card for the Week 4 loss:

Miami Dolphins rookies report card at Minnesota Vikings

Kadyn Proctor had a nice first-quarter trap block to help spring Ollie Gordon II for a first down run in the first quarter. Proctor has excellent movement skills, despite his enormous size.

While left tackle Patrick Paul struggled with four penalties in the first half, Proctor did not stand out for poor play. He can hold his own as a rookie.

The Dolphins had some big runs and were not terrible in pass protection.

Gordon posted his first 100-yard rushing game and scored a touchdown.

Chris Johnson made a great tackle on third down that appeared short of the marker but was awarded as a Vikings first down.

Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray was largely limited and rendered ineffective overall.

Jacob Rodriguez had a tackle on third down to get the Vikings off the field on their first possession of the game. Rodriguez made a nice third-down tackle of a receiver after a short gain in the first quarter, forcing a field goal attempt.

Rodriguez is an absolute tackling machine. He ended the first quarter with five total tackles.

Can winless Miami Dolphins upset undefeated Minnesota Vikings?

Chris Bell could not haul in a high pass from Malik Willis on third down in the first quarter.

Bell appeared to score a 68-yard touchdown in the second quarter after Malik Willis extended the play.

But was ruled to have gone out of bounds and re-entered play. A terribly bad break combined with the fact that Bell has to be aware of the sidelines.

Bell failed to haul in a deep ball that was broken up with less than six minutes to play and Miami trailing 15-10. It was a desperation throw into double coverage.

Kevin Coleman caught a short pass from Malik Willis late in the first quarter.

Coleman failed to haul in a deep attempt from Willis.

Will Kacmarek caught a short pass over the middle on Miami's first play of the game.

Kacmarek could not haul in a medium-depth pass at start of the second half.

Michael Taaffe started opposite Dante Trader at safety once again.

Trader was injured in the second quarter.

Taaffe was involved in some coverage against Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson, who had an outstanding game.

articles.title: Brad Marchand Returns to Florida Panthers, Sam Reinhart Moves to Center
articles.summary: The Florida Panthers are getting a big addition to their lineup just days after Sasha Barkov went down with a […]
articles.body:
The Florida Panthers are getting a big addition to their lineup just days after Sasha Barkov went down with a suspected left knee injury with Brad Marchand returning tonight against the Anaheim Ducks.

Marchand, 38, had surgery in August with coach Paul Maurice saying at the start of training camp that he would be out until November.

But Marchand looked and felt good enough in recent workouts , and got medical clearance, to come back sooner.

"It should be a great boost with Barkov being out of the lineup,'' Maurice said Sunday afternoon at Honda Center.

"He just brings so much energy … this guy is a really effective player. And he's a creative player. He's hard to game, and he creates from the chaos that he causes. … We're so pleased to have him back.''

On Saturday, Lars Eller moved up from the fourth line to take Barkov's spot centering the first — but Maurice said he is going to slide Sam Reinhart over to that position.

Marchand will replace Reinhart on the right side of the top line with Brady Tkachuk on the left.

The other three lines are able to remain the same.

Reinhart spent time at center with the Buffalo Sabres, including the second half of the 2021-22 season before being traded to the Panthers at the draft.

Florida has snot had much need to see Reinhart centering a line although Maurice said Sunday that the Panthers were looking to do so last season.

As the injuries mounted, the team decided against it.

"There was an idea last year if we could ever get Sam Reinhart into the middle of the ice,'' Maurice said. "We keep, in some ways, our center depth in term of veteran IQ. … It was in the back of our mind that if a center went down, Reinhart could be it. He came into the league as a centerman and was drafted very high. He might be our best option when we have the pieces.''

Defenseman Gus Forsling missed Thursday's game in San Jose after taking warmups. Maurice said he will be a gametime decision tonight.

articles.title: Instant analysis of Eagles' disappointing 24-20 loss to the Rams
articles.summary: Philadelphia finally generated takeaways, but its failure to protect Jalen Hurts and inability to sustain drives erased a promising first half
articles.body:
The Eagles had enough help to win Sunday. Their offense did not do enough with it.

Two interceptions, a 41-yard punt return from Britain Covey, and two touchdown catches from Darius Cooper helped Philadelphia build a 20-10 halftime lead. That advantage disappeared in a 24-20 loss to the Rams because the Eagles could not produce a single second-half point. In a similar showing for last season, Philadelphia gained 72 yards after halftime. Jalen Hurts completed two of nine second-half passes for 10 yards. The offense finished 0-for-12 on third down and converted just one of four fourth-down attempts.

The injuries matter in the end. Losing Saquon Barkley during a game already being played without Lane Johnson and DeVonta Smith reduced Philadelphia's options. But those absences do not eliminate the need for answers against pressure or explain every stalled possession. Nick Sirianni's failed fourth-and-goal gamble left the Rams within 10 points. The defense then surrendered touchdown drives of 98 and 79 yards. We'll discuss those breakdowns in length this week.

Still, Philadelphia repeatedly asked its defense to compensate for an offense that could not stay on the field. The Eagles found their first takeaways of the season and still lost. That is how costly their offensive problems have become.

articles.title: Cowboys rally behind Lamb's monster day despite poor defense, coaching
articles.summary: An awful first half, poor defense, and questionable coaching decisions weren't enough to keep the Cowboys from pulling off a dramatic win in Houston.
articles.body:
The Cowboys looked terrible in the first half of their Week 4 visit to Houston, allowing failures in all three phases of the game to put them in a double-digit hole at the break.

Whatever was said at halftime apparently lit some kind of fire. The second half was a very different story, with the Cowboys doing just enough- and several key playmakers doing much more than their share- to come away with a much-needed 34-30 win over the intrastate rival Texans .

Things got off to a rocky start, with Christian Parker's defense allowing a 45-yard catch to Nico Collins on the very first snap from scrimmage. Collins bookended the eight-play, 85-yard drive with a touchdown in what turned out to be a painful half to football for Cowboys fans.

The Texans scored on four drives over the first 30 minutes, twice converting failed long-distance Brandon Aubrey field goal attempts into easy threes of their own. Both tries- a 62-yarder that was blocked and a 65-yard try that went wide left- were highly questionable calls given the situation and will do head coach Brian Schottenheimer no favors this week as he continues to catch flak for his game-management decisions.

It was only the seven costly penalties by the Texans (for 51 yards) that kept their halftime lead to just 10 points.

But Dallas was a different team coming out of intermission, a big KaVontae Turpin kick return and a 49-yard drive combining for the Cowboys' first touchdown of the day just two minutes into the second half. The offense would find the end zone on three straight possessions after halftime, all Javonte Williams runs. It's the first three-TD performance for a Cowboys running back since Tony Pollard in 2022.

Williams racked up 62 yards on 19 carries, a solid day made spectacular by his three scores. Despite taking a cleat to the back of his throwing hand , Dak Prescott went 20-for-25 passing for 248 yards and a touchdown in the second half alone as he led the offense in the comeback. But Sunday's win will be remembered for CeeDee Lamb's monster day. More on that later.

The M*A*S*H unit that is the Cowboys secondary continues to struggle, giving up 347 passing yards and allowing Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud to post a 126.7 passer rating, one of the best games of his career. DaRon Bland and Reddy Steward in particular got victimized repeatedly, with Collins, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, Cade Stover, and ex-Cowboy Dalton Schultz all recording big-chunk pass plays that covered 20 yards or more.

The team's seven stops on 10 third-down tries look good in the box score, but the Cowboys defense did allow Houston to go 2-for-2 in the red zone, was unable once again to log a takeaway, and managed just two sacks on the day on 31 pass attempts by Stroud.

The decision to have Aubrey try those two 60-plus yarders in the first half will be called into question. But so will Schottenheimer's challenge of a pretty clear-cut Texans catch in the fourth quarter. He's 21 games into his career as a head coach and has yet to win a red-flag challenge. And the 3rd-and-1 short pass to Lamb that lost three yards might get overlooked by Jake Ferguson's catch to move the chains on the next snap, but the play call itself was befuddling. The only thing that might take even a scintilla of the heat off Schottenheimer this week is that he's not the most frustrating of the Cowboys coaches; the calls will grow even louder for Nick Sorensen's job after another week of poor special teams play.

In the end, the performance of the day belonged to Lamb: 17 catches on 21 targets, both career-highs for him, and the go-ahead final touchdown with 40 seconds to play. His 189 receiving yards were his third-best outing ever, and those 17 receptions are the second-best day ever in that category by a Cowboy. It was also Lamb's 30th 100-yard game, second only to Michael Irvin in franchise history. Lamb came into the game ranked top-6 in the league in catches, receiving yards, and touchdowns; his highlight-reel day in the city where he grew up and attended high school will certainly push him higher up that leaderboard once Week 4 has concluded.

articles.title: Instant analysis: Ravens survive Titans with bigger questions ahead
articles.summary: The Ravens improved to 3-1, but Lamar Jackson’s injury and 131 penalty yards complicated an afternoon that began with convincing dominance
articles.body:
The Ravens earned the result they needed. The performance left plenty to address.

Baltimore's 24-18 victory over Tennessee began with explosive offense and ended with Malaki Starks securing an onside kick. Between those moments, Lamar Jackson's ankle injury changed the game, and the Ravens repeatedly made their own assignment harder. Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. Baltimore scored touchdowns on all three red-zone possessions and did not turn the ball over. Those are winning contributions.

The Ravens also committed 13 penalties for 131 yards, handing Tennessee six first downs through flags. That is far too much assistance for an opponent that arrived without a victory. Without Jackson in the second half, Baltimore scored no points and opened with four consecutive punts. Tyler Huntley's eight completions in nine attempts show why the explanation has to extend beyond the backup quarterback. Protection, penalties, and the running game all belong in the discussion.

The defense forced two turnovers and limited Tennessee to two third-down conversions in 10 attempts. It also allowed a late touchdown that made the finish uncomfortable.

Baltimore is 3-1. That matters. Whether Jackson can play in Atlanta will matter even more.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo can return to Portugal team if he wants, says Jesus
articles.summary: Ex-Manchester United and Real Madrid star Cristiano Ronaldo left Portugal squad on Wednesday, but door open for return.
articles.body:
Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes, despite walking out on his teammates, national team coach Jorge Jesus said on Sunday.

The Portuguese showed they did not need the former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward as they became the first side to qualify for the quarterfinals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League with a 2-1 comeback win against Norway.

Goncalo Ramos secured the victory for his side in the 86th minute after Joao Cancelo’s powerful finish had levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener from outside the penalty area for World Cup quarterfinalists Norway.

After the game, Jesus said he was prepared to allow 41-year-old Ronaldo to return to the national team but that it would have to be the player’s decision.

“For me, Cris, in the next call-up, if he’s playing at Al-Nassr, he’ll be a player who can be called up,” Jesus told reporters, referring to Ronaldo’s Saudi club side. “If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team.”

The coach said he would speak with Ronaldo if he wished before Portugal’s next matches in November.

“If he wants to, as we did before this call-up, we talked before the call-up; we can talk before the next call-up,” continued Jesus. “But Cris is the one who’s going to decide.”

Ronaldo walked out of the national-team camp on Wednesday after a dispute over his selection by Jesus, leaving his international future in doubt.

Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most-capped player, Ronaldo was substituted in the Nations League opener against Wales on September 24.

He was then an unused substitute in the 2-1 victory in Norway on September 27.

When he was informed he would again be named on the bench for the match in Denmark, Ronaldo took a private flight back to Saudi Arabia.

Portugal went on to win 4-2 in Denmark on Thursday, while rumours swirled about Ronaldo’s departure and whether he would play for the national team again.

Ronaldo’s international teammate, Bruno Fernandes, spoke to the media on Saturday in the buildup to the return match against Norway in an attempt to settle a growing furore in Portugal about the matter.

“He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things,” Fernandes said.

“There are no divisions in the national team. It is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside…

“We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides, but at the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team; he deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less.”

Jesus had said he would speak about Ronaldo after Sunday’s match with Norway, but added in the buildup to the game that the forward is a “symbol of Portugal”.

The 72-year-old coach went on to say on Sunday that he had told Ronaldo he needed him in the squad for his first games at the helm after replacing Roberto Martinez following the 2026 World Cup.

“Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants; he’s the one who will decide how he wants it,” Jesus said.

“That’s how we talked, the two of us – I said, ‘I need you’. In my first call-up, I said, ‘I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you’. And now I’m saying the same thing.”

Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football.

The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.

Portugal host Denmark in their next international on November 14, before completing their Nations League group in Wales on November 17.

Ronaldo’s longtime rival for the title of the world’s best player, Lionel Messi, will play his final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: ‘Everyone knew’ – Marsch says relegation to follow
articles.summary: Jesse Marsch alleges Man City’s financial wrongdoing was widely known in the Premier League, and relegation must follow.
articles.body:
Canada coach Jesse Marsch has ‌called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League ⁠financial rules, saying his ⁠experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.

City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s ⁠financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the league alleging the club used “sham” commercial contracts to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn).

The club has denied wrongdoing, saying the verdict contained material errors of law, principle and fact, and filed an appeal on Thursday against the independent commission’s ruling.

Marsch, who managed Leeds United from 2022 to 2023, said the disparity between the clubs had been apparent to him during his time ‌in England.

“I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew,” Marsch told The Guardian in an interview published on Sunday.

Marsch also pointed to the 2022 summer transfer window, when Leeds sold Raphinha to Barcelona and Kalvin Phillips to City, while both clubs reported making money.

“That summer [2022], us and Man City were the only teams that said ⁠we made money,” he said.

“For us, we did make money, because we ⁠sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips. We had a lot left over from what we bought.

“At the time, we weren’t in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn’t have deep pockets. Whereas when ⁠Man City says this, I was literally like, ‘Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?'”

The American coach was also sceptical about ⁠City’s signing of Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund that summer.

“When ⁠they said they got Erling Haaland for 52 million pounds ($69m), it’s like, ‘Yeah, OK, sure!’ So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, ‘This is football’,” Marsch said.

City’s appeal will be heard privately by an independent three-member board, with the club fully denying all charges.

Potential sanctions include fines, points deductions and other sporting penalties, with relegation or ‌the ‌removal of titles also discussed as possible outcomes. It remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before the appeal is decided.

articles.title: Israel face spitting allegation as Ireland boss ‘delighted’ games are over
articles.summary: Ireland manager says ‘disciplinary committee will look at’ allegations Israel player spat at one of his coaching staff.
articles.body:
Tempers flared ‌again as Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 on Sunday in the second of their two UEFA Nations ⁠League meetings, concluding a fortnight ⁠dominated as much by political tensions as football.

Ireland had faced calls from some supporters and politicians to boycott the fixtures before beating Israel 3-0 behind closed doors in Hungary in their first meeting ⁠a week ago.

“I’m absolutely delighted this is finished,” Ireland’s Icelandic coach Heimir Hallgrimsson told reporters.

“It’s taken a toll out of us all. I’ve given so much credit to the players. They have been absolutely amazing in tough times, and I ⁠wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks.”

Ireland is one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, and the Football Association of Ireland chose to stage Sunday’s match behind closed doors in Serbia amid the pressure to withdraw from the fixtures.

The absence of supporters, however, did little to ease the tension on ‌the pitch.

Irish media reported that one of Ireland’s coaches, Damien Doyle, had accused an Israeli player of spitting at him after the half-time whistle.

Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match news conference, Hallgrimsson declined to provide details.

“I was there. I’m not going to comment. It’s something a disciplinary committee will look at,” he told reporters.

Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened.

“Halftime, I was in the dressing room, in my room with my ⁠staff; I didn’t see anything. When I’m going to see and check, I will get ⁠back to you with the answer,” he told reporters.

Tense Ireland-Israel atmosphere again in Nations League

As in the first meeting, there were no pre-match handshakes or exchange of pennants, while players from each team bowed their heads during the opposing national anthem.

Ireland again wore black armbands commemorating the victims of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza, ⁠with the Israelis sporting black armbands in memory of the victims of the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel that sparked the war.

Troy Parrott gave Ireland the lead with a 39th-minute penalty, ⁠but Dor Peretz levelled immediately after the break for Israel with their first ⁠effort on target.

Israel hit the woodwork twice in the second half of a poor game in which neither side could fashion a winner.

The draw left Ireland third in Group B3 on five points, three behind leaders Austria, with second-placed Kosovo ahead of them on goal difference. Israel are at the bottom with ‌two points.

Ben-Shimon welcomed his team’s response to the 3-0 defeat and rejected suggestions his players had been overly aggressive.

“When I come to a game, I say to my players, ‘This is the best way to play the cleanest football as ‌you ‌can, but be aggressive’, OK? I never say to injure someone; this is not our way. We are very human, human beings; we are very moral human beings,” he said.

articles.title: David Beckham’s £84M business empire makes almost £50M profit as his name becomes the product
articles.summary: David Beckham may have left professional football more than a decade ago, but his earning power has hardly slowed.
articles.body: David Beckham may have left professional football more than a decade ago, but his earning power has hardly slowed. His business empire has grown by doing something many companies struggle to achieve: making money without carrying the heavy cost of making products. Accounts for DRJB Holdings show £84 million in revenue in 2025, while pre-tax profit climbed to almost £50 million. The figures reveal a striking formula. Beckham is no longer simply selling his image. He has turned that image into a commercial asset that other companies are willing to pay heavily to use.David Beckham’s brand turns fame into a high-margin businessThe strength of Beckham’s business lies in what it does not have to own. His companies do not need to operate clothing factories, maintain large warehouses or take on the risk of unsold stock. Instead, partners handle production and distribution while Beckham provides something far harder to build: global recognition.DB Ventures remains central to that strategy, working on partnerships and licensing deals. Seven Global develops other Beckham-linked brands, while Studio 99 adds another revenue stream through documentaries, campaigns and media projects.That structure helps explain the extraordinary profitability. DRJB’s 2025 figures suggest that roughly 60p from every pound of revenue remained as profit before tax. For a business built around intellectual property and licensing rather than physical production, that is a powerful advantage.Beckham’s commercial reach also stretches across several industries. His name has been connected with BOSS menswear, Safilo eyewear and IM8 supplements, alongside partnerships involving brands such as Stella Artois, Maserati and Panini.The approach also limits exposure to some of the problems faced by traditional fashion and consumer businesses. Manufacturing costs, shipping delays and excess inventory largely sit with the companies making the products.David Beckham’s £200 million deal changed the scale of his empireA major turning point came in 2022, when Authentic Brands Group acquired a 55% stake in DB Ventures in a deal reportedly worth around £200 million. Beckham retained 45%, while gaining access to a company built around expanding celebrity brands through licensing.The financial benefits have continued. DRJB paid £38.9 million in dividends during 2025 and later approved a special dividend of £46.6 million. Beckham’s share of those payments was close to £38.5 million.That makes the business model particularly striking when compared with traditional fashion brands. His wife Victoria Beckham’s label has faced years of losses because it carries the cost of designing, producing and selling physical clothing.David Beckham’s empire takes the opposite route. It monetises reputation while partners shoulder much of the operational risk.There is still a clear vulnerability. A celebrity-led business depends on public trust and continued relevance. Beckham has maintained both remarkably well, helped by media projects, family visibility and his role around Inter Miami.His biggest business achievement may therefore have little to do with football. articles.title: 'I had fever, was not high on energy': R Praggnanandhaa after double medals at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In the open section of the 2026 Candidates Tournament, Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa was India's sole representative in Cyprus earlier this year.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In the open section of the 2026 Candidates Tournament, Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa was India's sole representative in Cyprus earlier this year. He did not win the top prize there. But the quality of chess he played was unmistakably high.He has continued to maintain that standard at every tournament since, and the results have simply followed.Despite being last at one point at Norway Chess, he made a remarkable comeback, beating five-time world champion and world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen twice on his home soil to become the first Indian ever to lift that coveted title in June.More recently, he became the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour. Coming into the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, nobody thus questioned his place as India's Board 1 player.And although he could manage only three wins from his 10 games during India's silver-and-bronze campaign, a tally that brought him an individual bronze medal too, there was never a lack of quality on show from the 21-year-old Chennai-born grandmaster."His score (6.5/10) still didn't completely reflect the level at which he played. He created chances in almost every game, quite a few draws which could have been wins. But the quality of his play was really high," captain Srinath Narayanan told TimesofIndia.com after the campaign. "It never looked like Pragg was in danger of losing. Even the couple of times he fought into slightly worse positions, body-language-wise, he was the one pushing. His opponents were the ones who were a bit stressed."The Uzbekistan Olympiad, though, wasn't an ideal one healthwise for much of the Indian contingent, and Pragg was among those who had to battle it out while under the weather.Fever, fatigue, and fighting through it"I'm recovering," he told this website, when asked if he was back to full health after the gruelling tournament, which had only one rest day. "The last few days I was having some cold and a little fever as well at some point. So I wasn't high on energy towards the end of the tournament. But it kind of got better after the tournament ended. The last few days have been better. I'm also getting good sleep, so it's fine."There was an obvious question about conditions, food, or the weather in Samarkand. Pragg waved most of that away. "I think the conditions were extremely good. The first day, we had a little inconvenience. But after that, the Uzbek Chess Federation arranged a private place for the Indian team to have their own dinner. We got the Indian food from the AICF, thanks to AICF, and we could keep it in this place. Generally, I think the overall arrangements after the first day were really good, thanks to AICF and the Uzbek Federation as well."So what was behind the string of illnesses, if not the food or the travel?"It was not a problem with any of those. I think it's just that something was maybe spreading among the players. I think it started with someone and then everyone towards the end got it." Asked if it was simply a viral fever making the rounds, he agreed. "Yeah, probably like viral fever that was spreading. I heard that even before the tournament, in my area and stuff, there were people who were getting it. But we were all fine in the first half of the tournament. It was mainly in the second half that these things started."It's rare, he insisted, for it to catch up with him specifically. "In general, I try not to experiment too much during a tournament. I go with my comfort food. I don't do something that brings a cold — even something like going out in the cold can trigger it. We also take medicines that usually don't make you sleepy, so you can be prepared in such a way. But generally, these things don't happen during a tournament. For me, I don't know when the last time was that I had a cold during a tournament. I can't really think of it. These things are rare for all the players. We're generally able to avoid these things, but it happens in some tournaments. Sometimes it's not in your control."A personal campaign that read better than the scorelineOn the board, Pragg's own account of his Olympiad matched what his captain had already said. "For me, I think I played well. Overall, the quality was okay. Most of the games I was pushing, I was the one creating a lot of chances. I think the only two games where I was worse were against Anish (Giri) and Rapport (Richard) in the last game. But it was only for a few moves. It's not like I had to defend for a long time. It was just a few moves, and then the position changed. Either I was fine or I was taking over."Where it stung was in the games he should have put away. "Given the chances I had, I could have, should have probably scored one or two wins more. Some games it was surprising how I missed. For example, the match against Spain, against Anton, I missed a completely winning position. That was kind of surprising to me as well. But these things happen in sports. Sometimes you convert these things effortlessly, but sometimes you also miss these chances. It all happens," the 21-year-old GM remarked.Where the gold went missingZoom out to the team picture, and Pragg is unambiguous about where the Olympiad was decided and at peace with how it ended."I think silver is a good result. Obviously, after coming from a gold medal last year and the way we won gold, there was an expectation from everyone, also from the players, that you're coming from such a high and you want to keep it. You want to win gold again. Obviously, repeating that performance is difficult, but you want to win gold again. But there are other strong teams, so it's not going to be easy every time. I think, in that way, silver is a good result. Given how strong the Olympiad was and how many close matches we had, I think silver is a good result," Praggnanandhaa explained.One match, though, decided it."Obviously, the critical match was against Uzbekistan. I think it's going to be the critical match in every Olympiad to come, because we're all strong players and we're all young, so there are going to be a lot of Olympiads where we will face each other. It's going to be interesting. But obviously, that match was the critical one," he said.Explaining what actually went wrong in it, he continued, "The Uzbek team also knew this was going to be like a final, because whoever wins has a massive advantage. One unfortunate moment (the queen blunder in Nihal Sarin's game against Uzbekistan) for us cost us the match, and these things happen in a tournament. But I felt overall, in that match, we were all playing well. Our game quality was really good. All of us were pressing at some point. We were not worse at any moment. There were no boards where we were in danger."One blunder can happen at any stage of a tournament, to anyone. I can show every top player blundering in some crucial game. It happens, and it's unfortunate that it happened at this moment. Obviously, it was difficult for all of us, but I think we all stood as a team. I think we recovered from that."Padel sessions between games, he added with a laugh, helped more than people might assume, "Yeah, I mean, especially for Nihal, it was more difficult, but I think we all managed to stay as a team, and I think we all are recovered now."I've been playing how I want to play. I've been enjoying playing the games, and I think it's also showing in the results.Candidates in the rearview, Clutch Chess aheadThe Olympiad arrives roughly five months after Pragg's own campaign at the Candidates in Cyprus fell short of the world title shot, a result that, by his own admission, shaped much of his year."It's been good these last few months. But obviously, I think the crucial tournament was the Candidates Tournament, which was a disappointment. After that, I felt my play has generally been good. I've been playing how I want to play. I've been enjoying playing the games, and I think it's also showing in the results."Does the Candidates setback still linger? "Not too much. I think these results do help in getting out of it completely. But of course, when you think about the future, Candidates is the main thing."For now, the schedule doesn't leave much room to dwell on it anyway. Pragg is already looking at his next two stops: Clutch Chess in the US, starting October 27, followed by the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot event in Budapest on November 10.A fever-interrupted Olympiad behind him, a title shot still unfinished business ahead, Praggnanandhaa feels his story has just begun.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: San Diego Padres blow late lead as star closer Mason Miller crumbles in brutal walk-off to Brewers
articles.summary: San Diego Padres trail 2-0 in the NLDS after Mason Miller walked three batters in the ninth to set up Jackson Chourio's walk-off two-run single.
articles.body: The San Diego Padres carried strong momentum into October after winning 20 of 23 games to finish the regular season and sweeping the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card round. That energy disappeared Sunday in Milwaukee. A 4-3 loss to the Brewers in Game 2 leaves the Padres trailing 2-0 in the National League Division Series and facing elimination. San Diego built an early lead behind RBI plays from Ty France and Dustin Harris. Milwaukee answered on Sal Frelick's RBI single and a Padres fielding error to keep the score tight. NO, THE SAN DIEGO PADRES DIDN'T LOSE BECAUSE OF CONTROVERSIAL NINTH INNING HOME RUN RULING Padres manager Craig Stammen turned to All-Star closer Mason Miller for a six-out save. Miller worked a clean 12-pitch eighth inning, but his command collapsed in the ninth. Miller walked three batters to load the bases without giving up a hit, setting up Jackson Chourio’s walk-off two-run single. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Miller was direct about his performance in the clubhouse after the game. "Terrible," Miller said. "I didn't do my job today, so instead of being in here with a win and a series tie, we're in a hole, so it feels pretty bad." Miller pointed directly to his loss of control in the final frame. "The cardinal rule is pretty much: You don't beat yourself. And I beat myself today," Miller said. "I mean, a base hit with nobody on doesn't win them the game. A base hit after you walk the bases loaded does." Stammen defended using Miller for two innings. "Top of the lineup in the eighth probably made that decision for Mason," Stammen said. "Going into the game, we were thinking of Mason for six outs anyway, especially how quick the eighth inning went for him. He was just battling the strike zone there at the end." PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG, CUBS OFFENSE NO-SHOW AGAINST PADRES IN NON-COMPETITIVE POSTSEASON EXIT The Padres locker room was all out of funk after the game, and for good reason. San Diego had World Series aspirations coming into October, but Milwaukee flexed a better killer instinct to tear them to shreds. Game 3 is Tuesday at Petco Park. Down 2-0, San Diego must win three straight games to keep its season alive. articles.title: New beginnings, new heroes: Women lead India's charge as a new generation shines in Nagoya
articles.summary: As Neeru Dhanda led the Indian contingent out for one last time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday night, it was symbolic of how India’s Asian
articles.body: As Neeru Dhanda led the Indian contingent out for one last time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday night, it was symbolic of how India’s Asian Games campaign had unfolded over the past two weeks.The women had come to the fore - packing punches, vaulting to new heights, lifting weights, taking aim, towering over opponents with sixes, blazing the track, finding the fairway and hitting the back of the net. India’s final tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, may represent a drop from the 106 medals and 28 golds won in Hangzhou. But numbers alone cannot tell the story of these Games.There were path-breakers everywhere, athletes who pushed through glass ceilings that had stood for years. The aftermath will bring reviews, reflections, deliberations and reports. But before the analysis begins, it is only fair to celebrate those who made these Games count.For almost 12 days, the Indian gold rush had remained subdued. Then, just as the sun finally began showing up in Nagoya, the floodgates opened. Eleven gold medals came in the final two days, transforming what had threatened to become a disappointing campaign into a collection of stories about guts, resilience and glory.Dhanda, the 26-year-old from Sangatpura in Haryana, had set the tone by winning India’s first individual gold of these Games in the women’s trap event. The women went on to win 11 gold medals, apart from the three secured in mixed events.The contingent had 83 debutants, who accounted for 41 of India’s 85 medals — a clear indication of a changing guard across several sports.But if one athlete were to be picked as the face of that change, it would be difficult to look beyond 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod. The Maharashtra archer won two gold medals and a silver, but her biggest achievement went beyond the medal tally.She ended South Korea’s two-decade domination of the women’s recurve events by becoming the first Indian to win individual recurve gold at the Asian Games. It did not take her long to make the biggest stage of her young career her own.Even her Korean opponent Oh Ye-jin, whom Kumkum beat for the individual gold, was left impressed. “For a 17-year-old, she is very composed and has a very bright future,” Oh said.Another teenager, Prithika Pradeep, also emerged with two gold medals, adding to the sense that a new generation is beginning to announce itself. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf gold.Behind every medal was a story of humble beginnings, survival in sport, societal pressures overcome and personal tragedies endured. That made the successes more than just entries in a medal table.The comeback girlsThey were not newcomers to the big stage. They had competed at the biggest of them all — the Olympics. But Nagoya offered unfinished business.Lovlina Borgohain had contemplated walking away from boxing after a difficult phase post the 2024 Paris Olympics. Instead, she returned to punch her way to gold.Parveen Hooda, returning after a doping ban, produced her own golden comeback. The bronze she had won in Hangzhou and subsequently lost became gold in Nagoya.Mirabai Chanu did not win gold, but her silver in the 49kg category had the weight of a champion’s achievement. It also completed her Asian Games medal collection.Golden standardsThe women’s kabaddi team survived a tense battle against Iran. The women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold. And Harmanpreet Kaur and her team ensured that cricket’s gold returned to India.Among the men, too, there were performances that demanded attention — Aman Sehrawat in wrestling, Ankush Panghal in boxing and Gulveer Singh in long-distance running among them.Yet, for all the celebration, there were glaring blanks. Manu Bhaker, one of India’s biggest sporting heroes, returned without a medal.There were plenty of nearmisses and some disastrous outings. India’s badminton return of a solitary bronze was another disappointment, particularly with a strong men’s doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen in the squad.Table tennis also raised questions, while equestrian had its own share of run-ins between administrators and riders, alongside selectionrelated concerns but failed to add to the medal count.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: Japan signs off, Doha takes the 2030 baton
articles.summary: NAGOYA: It has been a testing three weeks for Japan.
articles.body: NAGOYA: It has been a testing three weeks for Japan. Accommodation woes, transport and logistical nightmares, mismanagement and weather that refused to cooperate – the challenges the Asian Games organisers faced were plenty.Yet, as the Games drew to a close, there was enough to celebrate. Records were broken, medals won, friendships forged and, on Sunday, the baton was passed to Doha as Japan bid farewell to representatives from 44 countries at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.India finished fourth in the medals tally, while China topped the standings by a distance, collecting 341 medals, including an astonishing 169 golds.Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani described the Games as an event that would “shape the next generation of Asian sport” before welcoming the next chapter to his home country.“Tonight, as we lower the flag on Aichi-Nagoya 2026, we close these Games, but we raise the bar for Asian sport,” he said.“Over 350 records have been broken, including more than 50 world records. Forty out of the 45 NOCs achieved medals. This is a record for our Asian Games,” the 40-year-old added.In a symbolic handover to the next hosts, Qatar’s equestrian rider Jassim Al Kuwari, entered the stadium on horseback and received the OCA flag on behalf of Doha, which will host the 2030 Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The road to LA 2028: How Sjoerd Marijne and his team rebuilt India's women's hockey side
articles.summary: At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, tears flowed freely on the pitch.
articles.body: At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, tears flowed freely on the pitch. More than 5,500km away, in India, women’s hockey’s loyal legion, small in numbers but deep in investment, rejoiced.They had watched a team in which skill was matched by fitness, individual brilliance was backed by teamwork and, finally, belief had returned.The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented.Interest in women’s hockey had gathered pace after India’s fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics. Missing out on Paris, however, dented the hopes and aspirations that had begun to build.Then came the well-documented rifts, allegations, a dip in form and a spate of injuries. The shadow over Los Angeles grew darker.Enter Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff. They did not have a magic wand to make the demons disappear. What they brought was a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.The Dutchman was quick to point out that rebuilding a team is never the work of one person.“There’s a great connection among the staff and the players. I’m doing the interviews, but it’s an achievement from the whole staff. I’m really happy with all the quality I have around me,” he said.But there was another requirement, ensuring the players were fit enough to play as one.That was where Wayne Lombard, the team’s head of athletic performance, came in. He had a broad idea of the physical state of the squad when he arrived.The support staff hit the reset button. Rodet Yila and Caira Yila were brought in as scientific advisers, while the immediate priority was not fitness for fitness’ sake, but getting the players healthy.“Regardless of what the fitness levels were, the priority was to address the injury concerns,” Lombard said.That required more than exercises and numbers. The players had to believe in the process.“We had to sit down with the players and earn their buy-in. Helping them understand that the physical side of the game is every bit as important as the technical and tactical side,” Lombard said.He introduced the 30-15 intermittent fitness test to establish the players’ maximum aerobic speed. The test required them to run for 30 seconds, rest for 15 and progress across a 40m grid, with the speed increasing by 0.5kmph at every stage.Muscle by muscle, the players rebuilt their strength. With it came confidence.As the year progressed, India began to look increasingly like a team t rather than a collection of talented individuals.Poetic justice or coincidence, Japan had stood in India’s way in the qualifiers for the Paris Olympics. articles.title: Kyle Shanahan details knee injury for 10-time Pro Bowler
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers may be without one of their offensive staples for a period of time, but it sounds like they avoided catastrophe.
articles.body:
There was a scary moment for the San Francisco 49ers and fullback Kyle Juszczyk right when their offense got rolling Sunday vs. the Denver Broncos .

Brock Purdy rolled to his left and found Juszczyk all alone down the left sideline for a 16-yard completion. Broncos CB Jahdae Barron who tackled Juszczyk hit the fullback in the knees and caused Juszczyk's knee to hyperextend. Trainers tended to the 10-time Pro Bowler and needed to help him as he gingerly walked off the field. He was ruled out a short while later.

While it wasn't necessarily good news, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters after Sunday's game that Juszczyk appears to have avoided a catastrophic injury.

"Juice, we don't know for sure," Shanahan said. "They're thinking it was probably a knee sprain. His ACL and stuff looked intact, but to find out for sure we'll have to find out tomorrow."

Shanahan will speak with reporters Monday and have more information on what additional tests showed on the fullback's knee.

Ideally the 10-time Pro Bowler won't miss time, but the 49ers may have to figure out life without him for some period. Tight end Brayden Willis was next up as Juszczyk's replacement and it remains to be seen how long he'll need to play that role.

Juszczyk this season is playing 50 percent of the offensive snaps. He has three catches for 43 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Clippers rookie stuns Warriors with cold-blooded game-winner in preseason
articles.summary: Keaton Wagler showcased flashes of his potential in his preseason debut, leading the Los Angeles Clippers past the Golden State Warriors 104-101 on Sunday ni...
articles.body:
Keaton Wagler showcased flashes of his potential in his preseason debut, leading the Los Angeles Clippers past the Golden State Warriors 104-101 on Sunday night.

Wagler is gearing up for the rookie campaign of his NBA career following a great collegiate career at Illinois. Los Angeles liked his talents, selecting him fifth overall in the 2026 draft.

In 30 minutes of action off the bench, Wagler had his moments. He finished with a stat line of 15 points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals, and one block. He shot 3-of-15 from the field, including 1-of-11 from beyond the arc, and 8-of-9 from the free-throw line.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While he had an off night shooting the ball, one of the three shots he made ended up being clutch. Los Angeles trailed 101-100 with than less 15 seconds to go as Wagler pulled off some fancy moves before making a stepback jumper to put his team up for good.

How Keaton Wagler, Clippers played against Warriors

Keaton Wagler will hope for a better shooting display in the next contests. Nonetheless, he helped the Clippers secure the win over the Warriors to start the preseason schedule.

Los Angeles controlled the game for stretches, even leading 55-43 at halftime. Golden State fought back with runs of their own before taking the lead, resulting in Wagler's clutch highlight in the last 20 seconds of the night.

Three players scored in double-digits for Los Angeles in the win, including Wagler. Rui Hachimura led the team with a stat line of 21 points, five rebounds and a block. He shot 8-of-11 overall, including 4-of-5 from downtown. Darius Garland came next with 15 points and six assists, while Baba Miller provided nine points and six rebounds.

The Clippers will look forward to their next preseason contest, facing the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 10 at 6:30 p.m. ET. Their regular season starts at home against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 21 at 10:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Golden Knights hang on to continue dominance over Canucks
articles.summary: VANCOUVER—It should be no surprise that the Vegas Golden Knights have displayed dominance over some of their Pacific Division foes, due to how long they have...
articles.body:
VANCOUVER—It should be no surprise that the Vegas Golden Knights have displayed dominance over some of their Pacific Division foes, due to how long they have remained at the top.

While the San Jose Sharks have been well-publicized, an opponent that has gone more under the radar in terms of Vegas dominance is the Vancouver Canucks. Heading into Sunday night, the Golden Knights had put up seven straight wins over the Canucks. However, the Canucks were starting the season hot with 17 goals in three games, and they were hoping the performance would carry over.

The Golden Knights were much more prepared, however, and they pushed their win streak over the Canucks to eight with a 3-2 victory at Rogers Arena.

Despite starting out strong, the parade to the penalty box for both teams would stifle the early rhythm of the Golden Knights. The Canucks would be the first team to take advantage of the jumbled situation, however, thanks to former Golden Knight Paul Cotter tipping the puck on a power play at the end of the first period.

It would do little to deflate the Golden Knights however, who responded in dramatic fashion in the second half.

The ice would begin tilting thanks to Mitch Marner, who waited for Kevin Lankinen to sprawl before firing it into a yawning cage to tie the game at one.

"I liked our line for the last couple games," said Marner on his line with William Karlsson and Brett Howden.

"It just feels good to be rewarded as a three-man line out there. All three of us really take a lot of pride in how hard we work and how hard we make it for the other team to get through us."

Shortly after, the Golden Knights would switch back to a five-forward power play setup, swapping Shea Theodore with Victor Olofsson so Mitch Marner could return to the point. The decision worked out, as Olofsson was able to corral a pass from Mark Stone and pull the trigger while Lankinen was out of position, giving Vegas the lead for the first time.

"Just though we'd switch something up, try to give us some different energy on the power play," said Golden Knights head coach Ryan Craig on the adjustment.

While Jonathan Lekkerimaki would help the Canucks pull even after a shot from a bad angle ended up slipping through Adin Hill and into the net, the Golden Knights would respond just 34 seconds later. The fourth line would do their job and create some energy by crashing the net, allowing Marc Gatcomb to get a point-blank look for his first goal as a Golden Knight.

"I thought our fourth line was really good today," said Craig on the play of Gatcomb, Nic Dowd and Braedan Bowman.

"They're starting to form a bit of an identity with that line, knocking down pucks. There's some trust being built there with each other and, I think, with our team."

From there, the Golden Knights would rely on their defense and forechecking to lock down the Canucks. Despite Vancouver landing 10 shots in the last 20 minutes, they were unable to find the equalizer, giving Ryan Craig his first road victory as an NHL head coach.

Hill was able to close the door after the second goal was not to his liking, finishing the night with 17 saves on 19 shots.

"I think Hilly would be the first to tell you that he didn't like that second goal. I think what I liked was our team picked him up and scored right after that," said Craig about the team rallying around Hill.

"I thought when we needed Hilly to make some saves, he was there. Good win by our team, good win by Hilly and now we move on."

The Golden Knights will remain in the Pacific Northwest, when they finish the quick road trip against the Seattle Kraken on Tuesday.

articles.title: Will Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur consider a QB change after loss to Giants?
articles.summary: EAST RUTHERFORD — The Arizona Cardinals are reeling from a third straight loss, with Sunday’s coming against the New York Giants as questions continue to ris...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD — The Arizona Cardinals are reeling from a third straight loss, with Sunday's coming against the New York Giants as questions continue to rise about the quarterback position.

What was head coach Mike LaFleur's answer when asked about the idea of making a change at quarterback?

"No," LaFleur said to the media postgame.

The answer came after quarterback Jacoby Brissett's three-interception game, with the final one being a 98-yard pick-six by Giants cornerback Deonte Banks that ended the Cardinals' last chance in a 36-24 loss. Arizona has now fallen to 1-3 after opening LaFleur's tenure with a win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

The Cardinals have shown flashes offensively but have struggled with consistency, and Sunday's collapse turned what looked like a potential comeback into another frustrating loss.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) passes the ball, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Credit: Kevin R. WexlerNorthJersey.com / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards and two touchdowns against New York. Still, the three interceptions, including the final one, proved costly. LaFleur, however, put the interceptions in context, noting that the first two were tipped before saying the team needs to "improve" in those situations.

After taking over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback this season, Brissett has been inconsistent. He threw for 280 yards and two touchdowns without an interception in last week's loss to San Francisco, after passing for 95 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Seattle. He also threw for 277 yards and a touchdown in Arizona's season-opening win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Oct 4, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images

Through four games, Brissett has completed 103 of 152 passes for 818 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions.

The Cardinals have veteran Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck behind Brissett, but LaFleur has made it clear neither will take over — for now.

articles.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Reveals Kyle Juszczyk Injury Update After Win vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Stop me if you’ve heard this before: the San Francisco 49ers have suffered another potentially significant injury. The 49ers have yet to finish a game this s...
articles.body:
Stop me if you've heard this before: the San Francisco 49ers have suffered another potentially significant injury.

The 49ers have yet to finish a game this season without losing an integral contributor on either side of the ball.

In wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, and Arizona Cardinals, tight Jake Tonges suffered a season-ending MCL injury, rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suffered a torn deltoid that's expected to sideline him for double-digit games, receiver Demarcus Robinson suffered a high-ankle sprain that will keep him long-term, WR Mike Evans suffered a significant rib injury, and offensive tackle Trent Williams, linebacker Dre Greenlaw, and others left games with various injuries.

Moreover, in Sunday's 24-14 Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos, the 49ers lost another key offensive player to a concerning injury.

Kyle Shanahan Drops Kyle Juszczyk Injury Update

Late in the fourth quarter, Pro Bowl fullback Kyle Juszczyk exited the game after taking a brutal hit by Broncos rookie cornerback Jahdae Barron, who went low and drove his shoulder into Juszczyk's right knee.

After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to reporters that Juszczyk is dealing with a knee sprain and that his ACL "appeared to be intact."

"An MRI awaits for 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk tomorrow," David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard posted on X. "The team will hold its breath and hope for the best there. Juszczyk is a massively important player on the NFL's best offense"

Additionally, sports doctor Nirav Pandya noted that Shanahan's update confirms the 49ers training staff did a specific ACL exam in the locker room.

"Re: the Kyle Juszczyk knee injury: Typically when it is reported as a sprain and the ACL is 'intact' immediately after the game, this is based on physical exam testing that looks for ACL laxity in the locker room. An MRI is still needed to confirm the diagnosis."

articles.title: Chargers most to blame for brutal 0-4 start after comeback vs. Seahawks falls short
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers have officially reached crisis territory. Sunday’s 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a devastating summary of everything that h...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have officially reached crisis territory. Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a devastating summary of everything that has gone wrong during their 0-4 start. The Chargers dug themselves an enormous hole, fought courageously enough to make the game competitive, then watched the comeback disappear when Justin Herbert was strip-sacked with 54 seconds remaining. Los Angeles has now lost its first four games for the first time since 2017. The fight is there, but the execution has not. Right now, this season is in serious danger of becoming irrelevant before October is even halfway finished.

Sunday's defeat began with historic madness. Herbert was intercepted on the opening snap by Drake Thomas, only for Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold to throw an interception on the Seahawks' very next play. That allowed the Chargers to take an early 3-0 lead. Special teams disaster then struck when Derius Davis muffed a punt. That gave Seattle a short field that produced a 23-yard touchdown pass to Emanuel Wilson. Herbert later threw another interception to linebacker Ernest Jones IV before Seattle stretched its advantage to 27-6. To their credit, the Chargers fought back. Herbert found Kimani Vidal for a touchdown. Omarion Hampton added a two-yard scoring run. Cameron Dicker's field goal cut Seattle's lead to seven with just over two minutes remaining. The comeback, though, ended when Uchenna Nwosu strip-sacked Herbert and Derick Hall recovered. Herbert finished 19-of-31 for 189 yards. He had one touchdown and two interceptions while losing a fumble.

There is no questioning Herbert's arm talent, toughness, or importance to the franchise. That said, an elite quarterback cannot continually compound the mistakes surrounding him. Against Seattle, Herbert committed three crucial turnovers. He also struggled to generate consistent downfield rhythm. His 189 passing yards represented only 6.1 yards per attempt. Meanwhile, Seattle repeatedly pressured him into uncomfortable situations. The Seahawks sacked him four times, too. Herbert's 12 sacks through four games now rank among the season's worst.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Chargers need their franchise quarterback to become the stabilizing force when everything around him gets chaotic. Instead, the turnovers have magnified every other weakness.

Herbert obviously cannot and should not shoulder all the blame. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel deserves considerable scrutiny for his uneven offense. McDaniel arrived with enormous expectations. Four games into the experiment, though, and Los Angeles remains remarkably inconsistent. The offense has struggled to establish rhythm. The quarterback frequently appears disconnected from the structure around him. Even McDaniel has publicly taken responsibility for the unit's problems. Meanwhile, head coach Jim Harbaugh has insisted the coordinator's job is safe .

The Chargers actually discovered some offensive momentum after halftime against Seattle. They outscored the Seahawks 17-10 in the second half. Their running game even provided legitimate signs of life. Hampton finished with 45 rushing yards and a touchdown. Keaton Mitchell added 39 yards.

Yet Los Angeles still spent too much of the game asking Herbert to rescue an offense that had repeatedly stalled. McDaniel's system was supposed to create easy answers. Instead, the Chargers are still searching for them.

Maybe the biggest issue on the field is their protection problem. It would be unfair to blame one interior player or one specific alignment for Sunday's collapse, though. Left tackle Rashawn Slater, right tackle Joe Alt, and left guard Trevor Penning all left the game, after all . This forced Los Angeles to finish with three backup offensive linemen.

Now, Herbert was already under pressure before the injuries accumulated. Once Seattle could attack a compromised front, the quarterback's margin for error effectively disappeared. The final strip-sack was therefore not some random unfortunate play. It was already forthcoming. The Chargers just cannot expect Herbert to consistently operate under siege and still produce elite football.

Ultimately, the buck stops with Jim Harbaugh. He was hired to establish discipline, toughness, and accountability. Instead, the Chargers are 0-4 after another game featuring turnovers, special-teams mistakes, penalties, and a fourth-quarter collapse. Sunday's game included 30 accepted penalties for 280 yards between both teams. Los Angeles committed 16 of them.

That is not the culture Harbaugh promised. To his credit, Harbaugh praised the team's fight after the loss. Of course, fight without execution eventually yeilds diminishing returns. The Chargers now return home to face Denver in Week 5. There is no more room for moral victories. Herbert must protect the football, McDaniel must simplify and sharpen the offense, and the coaching staff must find a way to survive the mounting injuries. At 0-4, Los Angeles does not need another comeback. Rather, this team badly needs a transformation.

articles.title: Canucks Insider Links Elias Pettersson To Eastern Conference Club
articles.summary: One of the players the Vancouver Canucks chose not to trade last season was Swedish forward Elias Pettersson, who remains with the club despite the departure...
articles.body:
One of the players the Vancouver Canucks chose not to trade last season was Swedish forward Elias Pettersson, who remains with the club despite the departures of Quinn Hughes, Conor Garland, Tyler Myers, and Kiefer Sherwood.

However, that hasn't stopped the trade rumors from persisting. And now, a noted Canucks Insider is linking Pettersson to an Eastern Conference club that is going to have to start thinking about the future sooner rather than later.

Vancouver Canucks Insider Links Elias Pettersson To Eastern Conference Club

According to noted Canucks insider Rick Dhaliwal, the Penguins have a level of interest in acquiring Pettersson.

"I do believe Pittsburgh has some degree of interest in Elias Pettersson. I am not hearing the rumour that the Canucks have asked for Ben Kindel; no way the Penguins are gonna give up such a promising young player… for a bad contract," Dhaliwal said.

"Teams that are desperate at center call; I checked in this morning, Pettersson has not been asked… to waive his no-move; that tells you… there's nothing close," Dhaliwal added.

The Penguins, who still feature the legendary duo of future Hall of Fame forwards Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin, are going to need a source of offense when they both inevitably hang up the skates.

While there isn't any current traction on a move that would send Pettersson to the Penguins, it's apparently a move that could be considered at some point.

Elias Pettersson Plays At His Best When He Feels Comfortable With Himself

Pettersson, who spoke at length before the season began with new Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson , said that he feels he plays his best when he feels like himself.

"No, it means a lot. I mean, RJ is someone I've known for a long time, and he's always been a good guy for me," Pettersson said of his discussions with Johnson . "And it's been good just talking about the future, what he wants to see from me, and he makes you feel good. I play my best when I just feel like myself, but he's been good in that regard, and he just wants the best from you and wants everyone to be happy."
