articles.title: Dak Prescott throws for a season-high 355 in Week 4
articles.summary: Dak Prescott relied heavily on CeeDee Lamb en route to a Week 4 win over Houston, throwing for 355 yards and the game-winning touchdown.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown in a Week 4 win over the Houston Texans . He added seven yards on two carries.

Why It Matters: Facing a ferocious pass rush most of the game, Prescott was sacked three times, but he orchestrated an 11-play, 74-yard drive to win it. The drive included a fourth-down conversion and a 12-yard scoring pass to CeeDee Lamb with 40 seconds remaining. He now has eight TD passes to one interception this season. He's a QB1 in all formats, especially in Week 5 against Tampa Bay.

articles.title: Cowboys Face Mounting Calls to Fire Coach Despite Week 4 Win
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys got a win on Sunday, a much-needed win after Rio. But one coach is still facing calls to be fired. The post Cowboys Face Mounting Calls to...
articles.body:
Through four weeks of a particularly shaky Dallas Cowboys season, probably the only coach on the staff who can feel truly comfortable on his current perch is offensive coordinator Klayton Adams. The offense has scored 30-plus points in three straight games, after all, and because Adams does not have play-calling duties (which lie with head coach Brian Schottenheimer) he can hardly be held to account for some of the breakdowns that have occurred in that department. Schottenheimer, in his second season, is feeling heat. And defensive coordinator Christian Parker is, too, though he is still the new guy and would not be fired four games into his tenure. Nick Sorensen, on the other hand …

Sorensen is the special teams coordinator, and even going back to last year, there were questions about whether he would keep his job after Dallas struggled, on both sides, in the return game. This season got off to a rocky start, too, and a significant portion of the blame for the Week 3 loss to the Ravens lands on Sorensen. Not only was there a blocked field goal, but the Cowboys' final kickoff should never have gone for a touchback–the lack of a return preserved the seven seconds on the clock the Ravens needed to complete a pass and kick a field goal to defeat Dallas.

There were more Cowboys special teams mistakes on Sunday, too, including another blocked field goal and continued kickoff struggles. By Sunday night, even with the win over the Texans in Houston that brought the Cowboys back to 2-2, there was a loud chorus around the NFL calling for the Cowboys to make the move and fire Sorensen.

And not just random trolls on Twitter/X, either. Prominent Cowboys reporters and analysts were consistently bringing up Sorensen, who is in his second season in Dallas and just his second career stint as a special teams guy (2021 in Jacksonville).

Start with Cowboys beat reporter Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. He wrote, "Nick Sorensen's going to be on the hot seat after this game."

To that, longtime veteran beat writer Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys responded, "Should have been after last season."

Analyst John Owning posted during Sunday's game, "No idea why nick sorensen was brought back after last year tbh."

Kevin Gray of DLLS Sports agreed: " Nick Sorensen can go man, please."

Dallas sports anchor Brian Kolb posted video of the blocked kick and wrote, "The look on the face of Dallas special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen at the end…"

It would be unusual for the Cowboys to dump their coordinator at this point in the season. But, certainly, few would blame them if they did.

articles.title: Samford snaps ETSU Women’s Soccer’s winning streak, 2-0
articles.summary: JOHNSON CITY, Tenn. (WJHL) — ETSU women’s soccer saw its four-game winning streak come to an end Sunday with a 2-0 loss to Samford at Summers-Taylor Stadium....
articles.body:
JOHNSON CITY, Tenn. (WJHL) — ETSU women's soccer saw its four-game winning streak come to an end Sunday with a 2-0 loss to Samford at Summers-Taylor Stadium.

The Buccaneers and Bulldogs finished the first half scoreless. Samford appeared to take the lead in the final 30 seconds of the half, but Martha Bishop's goal was waved off for offside.

The Bulldogs broke through in the 59th minute when Becca Koenig finished a pass from Mamie Carman to give Samford a 1-0 advantage.

Brinley Murphy doubled the lead 11 minutes later, scoring on a header off a free kick from Caroline Smith to seal the victory.

ETSU outshot Samford 6-5, but the Bulldogs put five shots on goal compared with one for the Bucs. The loss snapped ETSU's four-game winning streak and five-game unbeaten streak.

The Bucs will play three of their next four games on the road, beginning Sunday, Oct. 11, at VMI. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. in Lexington, Virginia.

articles.title: Who were the top teen athletes at the Asian Games?
articles.summary: China’s Zhang Zhanshuo, 19, finished with seven gold medals while compatriot Yu Zidi won three record-breaking golds.
articles.body:
Teenage athletes have headlined some of the biggest Asian Games triumphs, leading their countries to historic gold medals, breaking records and cementing their legacy as formidable forces in the field.

Far from being intimidated by competitors double or triple their age, these schoolchildren remained cool and unfazed as they cruised to gold at their Asian Games debut.

Many are already familiar with the pressure and expectations of the world stage and have dominated their sport all season.

Al Jazeera Sport looks at some of the stars who left their mark in Japan:

At just 13, Yu was named female Most Valuable Player (MVP), as she bagged three gold medals and broke as many Asian Games records in a fairytale debut.

The schoolgirl stormed to victory in the women’s 200m butterfly, 200m and 400m individual medley (IM) and had a comfortable lead over her competitors.

Her time of two minutes and 6.10 seconds (2:06.10) in the 200m IM stands as a world junior record and second-fastest time ever.

“I don’t think I am what people describe as a prodigy,” she said after being crowned MVP. “I will continue to train hard, push myself and work alongside young athletes across Asia to inspire more young people to love and take part in sports, especially swimming.”

Zhang held up seven fingers after his 400m freestyle win to count out his gold medals at the Games – the most at this edition, and more than what 27 of the 45 participating nations had in their medal tally at the conclusion of the event.

He set Games records in the 400m and 800m freestyle, an Asian record in the 200m, and helped power China to gold and Asian records in the men’s 4x100m and 4x200m freestyle relays.

But the 19-year-old has bigger victories in sight.

“The Asian Games is not the goal. I’m still aiming for the Olympics and competing with the best,” he said.

The teenager’s haul helped China sign off from swimming with 30 golds out of 41 medal events in the pool, with chief rival Japan a distant second with seven titles.

Ohashi broke the world record in the men’s 200m breaststroke (2:04.83) in front of a home crowd to become the first swimmer under the 2:05 mark.

The gold added to his title in the 100m breaststroke shared with China’s Dong Zhihao, bronze in the 50m breaststroke, and silver in the mixed and men’s 4x100m medley relays.

The teenager said he was surprised and honoured that Olympic champion Leon Marchand knew who he was, after the Frenchman described the 17-year-old as a “scary” prospect ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

“I respect him because I know just how strong he is. But if I want to win, he’s someone I know I’ll have to beat.”

Ohashi’s world record performance came just a week after the teenager recovered from COVID-19.

Yan was already javelin world number one and Asian record holder when she stepped onto the field for her Games debut – her first and only throw of 70.46 metres was enough for gold and a Games record.

It was the sixth-best of all time and well ahead of Olympic champion and home hero Haruka Kitaguchi’s 62.70m.

Yan is closing in on the world record of 72.28m set by Barbora Spotakova in 2008. In May, she hurled a world-leading, record-breaking 71.74m to open an unprecedented season.

Chen stormed to a new Games record in the women’s 100m en route to her first gold as she announced herself as the new sprint queen in Asia.

“I have no limits,” was her response when asked how much faster she hopes to run.

She followed up her podium finish with a silver in the 200m and gold in the women’s and mixed 4x100m relays.

Goto narrowly missed gold in the men’s 400m hurdles, but his 47.93s was enough for a world under-18 best time, Asian under-20 best time, and a new personal best.

The teen star has run sub-50 seconds eight times this season alone, an impressive feat for a 17-year-old. His Asian Games silver added to the World Under-20 one he bagged in August.

Mohod scripted history for India when she became the first Indian to win an individual recurve archery gold at the Games. The 17-year-old helped India to gold in the women’s team recurve, and partnered with Dhiraj Bommadevara for mixed team silver.

Mohod’s gold was no stroke of luck; she defeated South Korea’s reigning world champion and Olympic medallist Kang Chaeyoung in the quarterfinals before dominating China’s Zhu Jingyi in the semifinals.

“Ever since I’ve made it to the national team, I’ve been visualising this moment. I had visualised shooting an X, and that is exactly what happened,” she told reporters after the match, according to Indian media.

World junior champion Anahat Singh has been India’s finest in the sport for several years now. Despite only being 18, Aichi-Nagoya was Singh’s second Asian Games outing after competing at Hangzhou 2023, where she won two bronze medals in the mixed doubles and women’s team events.

This time round, she won a silver in the women’s singles against world number five Sivasangari Subramaniam of Malaysia. However, her semifinal match against Japan’s Satomi Watanabe was what she called the “best win” of her career after producing a stellar comeback to defeat the world number six.

At just 11 years of age, e-sports prodigy Kurihara became the youngest gold medallist in Asian Games history when he won Puyo Puyo Champions.

“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” Kurihara said after his final, where he barely broke a sweat.

Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school – where he still studies – and soon started competing and winning in tournaments. He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults, often triple his age.

Ku took silver in the men’s skateboarding park with 87.33 points, and was just one of several teenagers – in his case, a pre-teen – who medalled in skateboarding at the Games.

Japan’s Izuru Nagahara, 15, took gold in the event. China’s Zhu Yuanling, also 15, won gold in the women’s street skateboarding competition.

China’s Cao Shiqi finished fourth in women’s skateboarding park and was the youngest athlete in China’s delegation at the Games.

articles.title: Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan talks about his awesome tribute to Steve Smith Sr.
articles.summary: Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan, in more ways than one, did his best Steve Smith Sr. impression on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers wideout Tetairoa McMillan just his best Steve Smith Sr. impression—in more ways than one.

The second-year receiver helped guide the Panthers to an impressive 32-26 win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday night—reeling in career-highs with 14 receptions and 192 receiving yards while tying another career-high with two touchdowns. But although he had already chalked up a two-score game twice before, this one looked a little different—or, to Panthers fans, quite familiar . . .

McMillan was asked about his tribute following the victory.

"I thought the camera had a mic," he joked. "I don't know why it didn't catch what I said. But I said, really, I said shoutout to Steve Smith. 'If you see this face, that means I scored, again.' So I did a little tribute to him, for sure."

That aforementioned stat line may also be a tribute to the franchise's all-time leading receiver. McMillan tied Smith's personal-best with his 14 catches and came up just nine yards short of Smith's 201, the regular-season franchise record, from 2005.

With McMillan seemingly reaching new heights early on in his second pro campaign, something tells us we'll keep seeing that face for many games to come.

Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content.

articles.title: The Rock Shuts Down WWE For Being Upset At His PAC Tribute
articles.summary: A wrestling report about WWE being upset inspired The Rock to speak against the reason for his company’s alleged displeasure. Rock recently posted a touching...
articles.body:
A wrestling report about WWE being upset inspired The Rock to speak against the reason for his company's alleged displeasure. Rock recently posted a touching video message to the wrestling community after AEW superstar PAC died. The video showed strong class with love sent to all wrestlers but an emphasis on Tony Khan and the AEW roster. Multiple tribute shows for two wrestlers who passed and one employee suffering from ALS weighs heavy on the AEW locker room dealing with heartbreak.

Rock replied in the Instagram comments about the report that WWE was upset:

"you're right brother, and humanity matters to me. I was born into this business and I've seen it all, but when one of our own passes away, I don't care nor do I see "our competition", I care about the wrestlers and how it affects them. I've been there. To me, humanity matters most."

It is worth noting that The Rock did not confirm or deny that WWE was unhappy with him. However, leaving an explanation does show that he felt the need to defend himself and shut down anyone upset at him. Most WWE and AEW wrestlers worked with PAC at some point to see all impacted and receiving Rock's compassion.

The Rock Chose Wrestlers Community Over Cold Executives

The main point made by The Rock is that he entered this industry as a wrestler, the son of a wrestler, and the grandson of a wrestler. Despite being part of the WWE board room, Rock understands what the performers are going through and the pain of this loss for hundreds of talents.

WWE's TKO ownership has taken a cold approach to pro wrestling with counter programing AEW and unofficially banning talent from mentioning them. Rock's post made headlines due to how unlikely it is for WWE talents to praise AEW and Khan by name in any public messages.

Nick Khan is the name that most holds responsible for the harsher business models involving AEW or even WWE's own talent. The new leadership to follow Vince McMahon believes in cutting budgets despite the record profits to improve their bottom lines.

Is There Tension Between The Rock & WWE?

The next big question comes from whether this becomes a problem between WWE and The Rock . However, this will likely just remain an internet story that the two sides never even address or talk about since it's all internet speculation.

Rock is often busy with his acting career and remains a WWE executive by proxy. The times where Rock returns in an on-screen role will see him then impacting the promotion more behind the scenes. Storylines involving Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes showed Rock's influence when he was part of the on-screen angles.

The next time that Rock is more involved in a hands-on role will come when he's likely part of the weekly television or at least at the events every week backstage. No one will have issues with each other, unless WWE directly expresses their opinion going against Rock to him.

articles.title: Cam Ward threatens to walk out of press conference after Tennessee Titans reporters get late
articles.summary: Cam Ward arrived a few minutes early to his post-game press conference, but didn’t appreciate having to wait for reporters. Ward and the Titans lost their fo...
articles.body:
Cam Ward arrived a few minutes early to his post-game press conference, but didn't appreciate having to wait for reporters.

Ward and the Titans lost their fourth straight game on Sunday, with their latest loss coming at the hands of Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens.

However, rather than his performance on the field, Ward's interaction with members of the press after the game has become one of the biggest talking points from the game.

Cam Ward demands reporters not make him wait in post-game press availability

During the post-game press availability, Tennessee Titans QB Cam Ward arrived at the podium before reporters were done speaking with other players in the locker room.

A visibly frustrated Ward noted that he had been waiting for three minutes and was ready to walk out if the reporters didn't come in time, even tapping on the podium to hurry them along.

"Well, ain't nobody here. We can just go… At least I'll get some good questions. They've got three minutes, bro. I'll walk out."

While Ward's frustration is somewhat understandable, his demeanour and tone cannot be justified. The reporters were not expecting him to arrive at the podium early and, understandably, were running behind when he demanded they ask him questions.

On top of that, Ward is a huge reason why the Titans are 0-4, yet he has shown very little frustration over their start, or even taken any of the blame for their losses.

For Ward to act like a superstar quarterback in front of the media without delivering the results needed to earn that status is not a good look.

Against the Ravens, Ward had an average performance, throwing for 222 yards and one touchdown. And while he did carry for an average of 6.8 yards across four carries, it wasn't a particularly impressive outing.

After what had been a disappointing first season, the Titans were hoping that Ward would take a huge leap this season and allow them to post a winning record.

Unfortunately, that just hasn't been the case. And until Ward can start delivering at a high level and bringing the Titans some wins, he should re-evaluate how he treats people around him.

articles.title: Javonte Williams has a career day in Week 4 against Houston
articles.summary: Javonte Williams posts 83 total yards and a career-high three touchdowns in Week 4 against Houston.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys RB Javonte Williams carried 19 times for 62 yards and a career-high three touchdowns in a Week 4 win over the Houston Texans . He added five catches on as many targets for 21 yards.

Why It Matters: All three of Williams' TDs came in the second half, as the Cowboys scored 28 points after the break. Dallas has struggled a bit in the run game in the early going; Williams has yet to surpass 64 yards in any game, but he now has four TDs and is a RB1 in most fantasy formats. That doesn't figure to change in Week 5 against Tampa Bay.

articles.title: Sam LaPorta hits pay dirt in Week 4
articles.summary: Targeted a team-high 13 times, Sam LaPorta finished with 84 yards and a score on eight receptions versus Carolina.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions TE Sam LaPorta posted eight receptions, 84 yards, and a touchdown during the team's Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers . He was targeted a team-high 13 times.

Why It Matters: Coming off an injury-shortened 2025 campaign, LaPorta had been mediocre through the season's first three weeks, averaging 48 yards per game and scoring once. On Sunday night, he enjoyed his best game since Week 9 of last year, posting an 8-84-1 line while leading the team in targets. Although LaPorta isn't on the level of Jahmyr Gibbs or Amon-Ra St. Brown in terms of priority usage from one week to the next, the former Hawkeye does enough to carry decent TE1 appeal.

articles.title: Rutgers Head Coach Greg Schiano and Indiana Head Coach Curt Cignetti Host Post-Game Press Conferences
articles.summary: Schiano discusses what went wrong, Cignetti discusses how Rutgers can become a winner.
articles.body:
Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano hosted a press conference with members of the media after the Scarlet Knights' 47- 15 loss to Indiana on homecoming. Without being prompted at the beginning of the press conference, Schiano said that he and the coaching staff need to make some "tough decisions" regarding the current team's capabilities.

Later in the press conference, when he was asked to elaborate on those changes, Schiano said this: "Anything's on the table. Like I said, I love the coaching staff, I love the players. It's not going to be any of that. It's going to be, what can we do better? We have to improve. I thought we did improve the last two weeks, and we didn't improve this week. Again, as I said, the opponent has something to do with that. My hat's off to them. They're a quality football team, and Coach Cignetti definitely had them ready to play tonight. They had an edge to them. You could see it, you could feel it. Early in the game, I thought we had some opportunities and we didn't cash in. You get behind a team like that and it's very hard. But again, like you mentioned, the defense, that's really difficult when you give up explosive plays like that. We didn't turn the ball over, neither did they. But explosive plays — it's hard when you give them up the way we did."

Now we know Schiano was never going to give any hints about what those changes might be, and it's not even clear whether or not he will be around to make them, but it will be interesting to see if anything actually does change in two weeks when Rutgers has its best chance to win another game this season against Maryland.

Much of Schiano's press conference was much the same; however, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti said something interesting when asked if his success over the last three years gives hope to a program like Rutgers.

"I think success starts at the top with a commitment and alignment. From the president to the athletic director, it takes a certain amount of financial commitment to be successful. It doesn't mean you have to be number one or in the top 10 in certain things, but you've got to be competitive, and that's what we've tried to do," said Cignetti. "I think Greg Schiano- what he has done at Rutgers- he's had two great runs; it's a little tougher around this time in the Big Ten. Can it get done? Yeah, I mean, it can get done. Greg is a great football coach."

articles.title: Who slept worst last night: an F1 fan
articles.summary: Formula 1 is booming but the Bahrain GP in Malaysia offered a reminder of why some long-time fans are wondering whether the series has gone a step too far
articles.body:
You know how you try to watch a series you like, but it's sort of a boring episode with a lot of nothing going on – at least in the beginning – and you fall asleep in front of the TV? And have trouble sleeping through the night afterwards...

Well, that could have been one of the problems last night for Formula 1 fans around the world who had to endure an almost hour-long break in the scheduled programme of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, seeing pictures of cars parked in the pitlane and mechanics wandering around. You wouldn't blame anyone for falling asleep, having woken up on a Sunday morning to watch their favourite motorsport fail to start on time.

There was a delay because of the rain, yes, but those who have followed F1 for ages surely wouldn't have been disappointed to see it pissing down when they tuned in. If you've been following F1 for about three decades, you surely know that feeling: it's a good one.

Television, dialled. Ear-pleasing guitar music, like a signal for lab rats desperate for their dopamine hit, quickly crescendos. The FIA logo with an F1 car incorporated into it assembles itself on your screen. And, when you see raindrops on the helicopter camera, blood instantly rushes to your brain.

Lab rats or not, you know - you just know - you're going to be treated to something special.

We've had rain delays in the past. They just added to the anticipation. They put you on the edge of your seat. F1 cars before battle, parked on a wet grid, were also a treat. The eyes of highly concentrated drivers with their helmet visors still up, staring ahead. Gladiators. Mechanics, whirring about, covering tyres with blankets. Engineers looking up at the skies. In the past, these were the best grid images ever, weren't they? Not the ones with endless singers, actors and influencers you couldn't recognise on a clear day, let alone in the rain.

It was always - and I mean, always - worth the wait. Because something amazing was about to happen.

Picture two Ferraris, those of Michael Schumacher and Rubens Barrichello , going off the track almost simultaneously at Sepang shortly after the start, unable to control their cars on the slippery surface — only to then put on an overtaking fest, climbing back through the field amid the complete chaos of the race.

A quarter of a century later, it was Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton crawling down the very same track at golf-cart speed during the formation lap ahead of a race that was about to become a thriller . Unable to control their machines with the throttle, the gladiators of modern Formula 1 appeared to be powerless, in every sense of the word. The thriller had to be red-flagged.

On this particular occasion, with this particular software glitch, which threw these super-complex power units into disarray, you deprived F1's most dedicated fans of something amazing.

It could have been a father delaying a trip with his family, for this. It could have been a kid for whom F1 is his own escape world. An old man in a retirement home who still remembers watching guys like James Hunt and Niki Lauda at Fuji fighting for the world title back in 1976.

"I wish we could go when we went, because you'd have had a nice race," said Alex Albon , an F1 driver and surely also an F1 fan himself, after the flag.

"The track was good enough to start on the wet tyres, to race under those conditions. It would have been nice to actually get proper running in the wet with these cars and these regs."

There was still a decent race, it has to be said. There was a battle at the front and an overtake for the lead, a back-to-front charge from Hamilton, mixed strategies, mistakes and some drama. It was just that it wasn't anywhere near what it could have been, leaving that sour aftertaste.

Russell felt this weekend's race day was a

George Russell summed it up pretty well.

"The whole day felt like a bit of a faff with the delay and then the red flag and then endless laps under the safety car," he said in the media pen. "It just didn't feel very F1 today. And I'd have been a bit disappointed if I was in the stands watching that unfold."

Formula 1 is booming. There's no doubt the series itself is in great shape. The best it's ever been. Brad Pitt is shooting a sequel to the F1 movie, after all! The Netflix series is still going strong, despite the predictable decline, but, as they say, still way better than other similar behind-the-scenes semi-documentaries about other sports.

It's also well known to those within the industry that F1's own fan surveys return good numbers on how exciting those taking part actually find the races. The stats do look good. But do they also reflect the way those who have followed F1 for decades actually feel?

The grass will always look greener if you close your eyes and remember the races from the good old days. There were a lot of boring ones as well. There's no doubt about that. But there were some bloody good ones, too! And it's those that stick in the memory best.

It's difficult to point fingers at anyone for that software glitch, which turned the hour before the actual start in Malaysia into an embarrassment. The FIA would be the usual punching bag, but first, it's not entirely its product and the software was developed together with the teams. And second, these PUs appeared in F1 for a whole lot of different reasons - commercial ones first and foremost, as the series was trying to please the car manufacturers.

They are powerful organisations, those OEMs, and there's ultimately nothing wrong with them being associated with F1 - because they do help this boom keep booming with their marketing machines armed with cash. They bring new fans. Allegedly, at least.

The 2026 race at Sepang still delivered a decent show

But it's those who have followed Formula 1 for decades who now ask themselves difficult questions about whether it's still the same series they grew to love.

It's them, the educated and knowledgeable fans, who cringe at seeing cars slowing down on the straights. It's them exhaling at power unit-assisted overtakes. It's them, the minority as it looks now, not enjoying it as much as they used to. And it's them who shake their heads in disbelief at what it's become, reading drivers' comments about how computers decide more than they should.

It's also true that not everyone cringes and shakes their head. But after the show F1 put on in the build-up to the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, a lot of those who actually don't mind the yo-yo racing are probably still asking themselves whether this regulation set is indeed a step too far.

"I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal, that was quite scary, actually," said Oliver Bearman after the race. "I don't think they should be able to turn off our throttle pedals. I know that wasn't the goal. And maybe it could be used for good things, like in a safety car or a red flag situation. If there's a massive shunt, turn off everyone's throttle pedal. I guess it's not a bad thing.

"But in that case, it probably tells us that maybe we've gone a bit too far in terms of intervention and this low-grip mode stuff, all of those things. It's a nightmare to understand."

I'm personally not a fan of drivers going out and slagging F1 off in the media, like they did at the beginning of the year. It would have been a lot better had those involved managed to keep the discussion behind closed doors - but maybe it's still not such a bad thing if someone like Verstappen speaks out if he feels these regulations are what actually threaten the future of the championship they love. We love.

These people used to be called petrolheads.

Verstappen's open criticism of F1 was strong, but maybe he had a point

It's also pointless to deny progress and new technology. The world is definitely changing, and F1 absolutely has to keep up with it.

But maybe it also needs to realise and admit it simply went too far. Or at least try to do some favours for those who represented the core of its fanbase when it wasn't exactly booming. It's not "bring back V10s", "ban computers" or "make everything like 2001". Maybe start with something small: make sure that when it rains, the best drivers in the world are still able to wrestle racing cars around a wet track.

And then maybe just make these cars a bit simpler themselves, so that no one has to second-guess whether it's the driver who made the difference or the algorithm that deployed a few more horsepower at the right moment. The petrolheads would definitely approve. And that wouldn't be such a bad thing either. Because, after all, it's them who are likely to stay when the boom isn't booming any longer.

articles.title: Dan Campbell 'not talking about' moving on from Lions DC Kelvin Sheppard
articles.summary: Dan Campbell is not ready to discuss firing defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard despite the Lions' defensive struggles.
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. — After another thrashing at the hands of his defense in a 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 4, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said he isn't ready to talk about the possibility of moving on from defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

With the Lions giving up 31.8 points per game through their first four games en route to a 2-2 record, Campbell said, "I'm not talking about all that," when asked how many more of these performances he can take before considering a change at defensive coordinator.

"I'm not talking about all that. I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got, and that's what we're gonna do," Campbell said. "We're gonna find a way to get better with what we have."

It wouldn't be unprecedented for Campbell to make this time of move. He took over play-calling duties from former offensive coordinator Anthony Lynn in the second half of the 2021 season and saw dividends paid as the offense turned things around and the team finished 3-3. In 2022, he fired defensive backs coach and passing game Aubrey Pleasant , leading to a turnaround with the secondary.

And just last season, he relieved former offensive coordinator John Morton of his play-calling duties after the unit was plagued with inconsistency following the departure of Ben Johnson.

Campbell said he reserves the right to consider a change down the line and will always do what he thinks is best for the team.

"I'm gonna always do what's right by this team, what I truly believe is the best thing and the right thing to do, always. I'm always going to do that, man," Campbell said. "That's the most important thing is what's right for the players, man, and what gives us the best opportunity to win."

Right now, the defense isn't giving the Lions a chance to win. They've held an opposing offense under 30 points just once through four games — and they allowed 24 points in that game, a win over the New York Jets in Week 3 — as the offense, though it hasn't been perfect, has largely been able to uphold its end of the bargain.

Multiple Lions players followed their head coach's lead and gave Sheppard a vote of confidence but acknowledged that something needs to change.

"I've been with Shep for years now, man," Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson said. "As an assistant and now as a coordinator for the past two years now — I have the utmost faith in him. I think we have the utmost faith in him. But yeah, definitely, we have to evolve as a defense, and we have to grow. Because we can't keep putting our offense in these shootout-like games. It just puts stress on them. We've just got to do better as a unit. I think we all ... support Shep fully."

Lions cornerback D.J. Reed, who's been at the center of Detroit's struggles in the secondary, said, "It's not a coaching thing."

"It's a players thing. This game comes down to winning one-on-ones, and that's what we gotta do as a whole collective unit," Reed said. "In the secondary, we haven't been doing that. So we just got to be better."

Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, one of Detroit's defensive captains, said, "It starts with the players," when asked about his confidence in Sheppard.

"We're out there and we make the scheme come alive, so honestly, put it on me. Put it on the players," Jack Campbell said. "But I mean, Shep — he works hard, Dan believes in him, I believe in him. He's made of the right stuff. We're gonna get this figured out. We just gotta stay the course, stick together, because right now, it's us versus everybody. I'll state the obvious: we're not playing very good defensively, and we gotta fix it."

The Lions have one more game until the bye in Week 6, which would be the optimal time to make a change at coordinator, if that were to happen.

articles.title: Swim challenge 'error' leaves man barely able to walk
articles.summary: Susanna Thorpe accidentally selected the longest distance for her husband's charity swim.
articles.body:
A man said he could "hardly walk" after completing a long distance cold water swim following his wife's keyboard error.

Mike Thorpe, 57, from Fyfield in Wiltshire, was planning to swim one mile (1.6km) in the Swim Serpentine at Hyde Park in London, but was forced to swim an extra five miles (8km) after his wife hit the wrong button.

Susanna Thorpe said her husband's achievement was "amazing", but she would not be forgiven "for a very long time".

Mike described the swim as "scary", but he was happy to have raised £4,500 for the Wiltshire Bobby Van Trust (WBVT) which supports older and vulnerable people.

Susanna had meant to click the one-mile (1.6km) option for six people but ended up booking the six-mile (6km) option for one person.

"My lovely husband turned around and said don't worry I've got this, I'll do it.

"He's not a natural swimmer and he's got a frozen shoulder...it was really hard," Susanna continued.

About 6,000 people took part in this year's Serpentine, but only 50 tackled the six-mile option.

He also has frozen shoulder, a condition that causes pain and severe stiffness in the shoulder joint, which meant he had to swim breast stroke rather than front crawl.

The water's temperature was about 16.9C (62 F) and Mike was "shaking so much" officials checked on him.

But with only one mile (1.6 km) to go, he decided to carry on.

For his training, Mike swam five days a week at the Marlborough Leisure Centre for four months, and also at Cotswold Water Park.

Mike, who chose not to wear a wetsuit, said he could "hardly walk" and was "staggering all over the place" at the end of the challenge.

"Half of it was fitness and half of it was grit...I underestimated the temperature of the water," he said.

WBVT director Jennie Shaw said, what Mike achieved was absolutely incredible.

"Taking on six miles of open-water swimming is no small feat, and we've been amazed by the determination, commitment and courage he has shown over the past four months.

"We're hugely grateful to Mike for taking on this 'accidental' challenge and raising vital funds for our charity," Shaw added.

articles.title: Dodgers know they must break their reliance on home runs to beat Braves
articles.summary: Freddie Freeman says the Dodgers need to overcome their reliance on home runs if they want to improve their chances of beating the Braves in the NLDS.
articles.body:
The most impressive number the Dodgers put up this season was 100 — the number of games they won. They had to do a lot of things right to get there.

No Dodger ranked among the top 16 in the majors in home runs or the top 30 in RBIs, yet they were fourth in runs scored. How? They were third in the majors in walks and near the bottom in strikeouts, which allowed them to manufacture runs by stringing together long innings rather than relying on the long ball.

Two games into the postseason, that script has flipped. After Sunday's 3-2 loss to the Braves, the Dodgers head to Atlanta with their best-of-five National League Division Series tied. Suddenly the Braves, who will start ace Chris Sale on Tuesday, have the edge.

"Getting the split in this place against these guys, yeah, it's awesome," Braves manager Walt Weiss said.

All seven of the Dodgers' runs in the NLDS have come on five home runs, three of them with the bases empty. When the ball stays in the park, the Dodgers are 0 for 9 with men in scoring position, stranding 13 runners. They've also struck out three times more often than they've walked and are batting .215 against the relay team of 10 pitchers Atlanta has used.

"We didn't throw out a bunch of hits, but there was still traffic," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "We didn't need many hits tonight to have a different result, and we just couldn't get it."

Sure it's a small sample; just two games. Yet it should be a troubling one for the Dodgers, the two-time defending World Series champions.

"Sometimes it's just you can't hit," said Mookie Betts , who walked twice. "I mean, there's nothing really you can do to explain that. You've just got to be in the moment and come through. We had some moments today [when] we didn't come through.

"That's part of the game. We've just got to keep giving ourselves moments, and eventually something will happen."

"We've to find a way to score some runs without hitting a home run," added Freddie Freeman , who homered Sunday and has three hits in the series. "That's our biggest thing right now. So keep getting guys on base and get that big hit."

Freeman said the Braves have done a good job keeping the Dodger hitters off-balance by emptying their bullpen, sending in a fresh pitcher every couple of innings.

"It's tough because you're facing a different arm every single time you're going up there," Freeman said. "It's different angles, different velocities, different things. So stringing hits together is very hard.

"This is the playoffs. We're not going to score eight to 10 runs. It's hard. Pitching staffs are good."

Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernández wondered whether the Braves' game plan might soon backfire. Aside from Sale, Weiss has few pitchers left the Dodgers haven't seen; eventually they'll catch up.

"Moving forward, just know that we've seen basically the best out of the bullpen," Hernández said. "We can have a better plan for Tuesday and Wednesday."

Although the Dodgers committed the second-fewest errors and gave up the fewest unearned runs during the regular season, they haven't looked sharp defensively in the postseason, with all three Atlanta runs Sunday coming with two outs.

The Braves loaded the bases in the first inning on a single and two walks before scoring when a diving Betts snared a Mauricio Dubón grounder up the middle, but threw wild and late to first, allowing Ronald Acuña Jr. to score. They then went ahead to stay in the fifth on a line drive to left that Hernández misplayed into a triple, followed by pitcher Kris Bubic's wild pitch.

"I didn't think he hit it that good," Hernández said. "I didn't break in, but I broke to the side. And then when I realized, it was too late."

Atlanta's final run came in the seventh when Michael Harris II one-hopped the wall in right-center, allowing Matt Olson, running from first on the full-count pitch, to score.

Now the advantage swings to the Braves, who go to Truist Park, where they had the second-best record in the National League.

"We knew it was going to be a battle. We knew those guys weren't going to go down," Roberts said of the Braves.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: France legend, coach has high praise for Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise
articles.summary: Zidane calls FC Bayern star “a natural leader with his game”.
articles.body:
France legend and current national team manager, Zinédine Zidane, is impressed with Bayern Munich star and France international, Michael Olise. Between UEFA Nations League matches in this international window, Zidane spoke to the media and commented on Olise's antics on and off the field.

Zizou, speaking to French media outlet Téléfoot (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), had this to say about Olise: "He's a bit reserved and shy off the pitch, but that's fine because on the pitch he's not shy at all – he's a natural leader with his game. He's showing all his talent with the ball. He has established himself here for a while and is doing very well at his club."

In three matches with France this window, Olise scored a goal in two of the matches and recorded an assist in the other. Since the beginning of this season, Olise has had a goal or an assist in all but two matches played for club and country in all competitions. France will host Belgium on Monday before Olise heads back to Bayern for a return to club play.

articles.title: Elfyn Evans defies history to join Britain's rally greats Colin McRae and Richard Burns with WRC title
articles.summary: Elfyn Evans has been the nearly-man of world rally until he finally emulated the feats of Colin McRae and Richard Burns.
articles.body:
For what must have felt like an eternity, Elfyn Evans feared history was repeating itself yet again.

At 3.05pm local time in Sardinia on Sunday, Evans could only stand and watch as another world rally title looked to be slipping from his grasp.

Evans was preparing in his head yet another runners-up speech - it would be his sixth - as he waited for Oliver Solberg to cross the finish line and be crowned world champion.

Of the five previous times he had been championship runner-up, three had been decided on the final day and twice after he had taken a lead into the final event.

But at 3.06pm, for once the motor-racing gods were on his side.

With just two turns to go on the final stage of the final round and with victory in sight, Solberg somehow careered off the track into the Sardinian sand to hand Evans his first world title.

In the most dramatic of finishes, the 37-year-old from north Wales became the first British winner of the of the World Rally Championship (WRC) in 25 years.

Only two British men had taken the title since the WRC's 1977 inception, matching the exploits of legendary pair Colin McRae (1995) and Richard Burns (2001).

Louise Aitken-Walker was Britain's first world champion when WRC ran a women's version in 1990.

As it happened: Evans wins title as Solberg crashes on final stage

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done," said Evans.

"It's been a difficult weekend. I felt on Friday things were slipping away. We were a bit powerless with the road position we had and Oliver was flying."

His experienced co-driver Scott Martin revealed Evans was already apologising for his stage performance as they waited for Solberg to finish.

"I've said all week that until we arrived at the beach after that last stage it was never over. How true that turned out to be," said Martin.

Evans and Martin have been consistent performers throughout the 2026 championship, through the streets of Monaco, the ice and snow of Sweden, the flowing roads of Chile, and the punishing, sun-baked gravel tracks of southern Europe.

Despite winning only two of the previous 12 events, the pair took a 21-point lead into the final race at Rally Italia Sardegna.

Solberg, whose father Petter won the 2003 title, was around one kilometre from glory only to suffer motorsport's version of Devon Loch.

"The lead up to this event gave us a bit of a buffer and we just about managed to hold on at the end. It was an incredible finish," said Evans.

"I feel for [Solberg] after he came so close and lost at the last moment. I've been in a similar situation and it will be tough for him for a few days, but he's shown he's one to watch for the future."

Evans, like Solberg, is also from fine rally driving stock. His father Gwyndaf was British champion, as well as runner-up four times, but the ruddy-cheeked farmer never got the break to complete on the world stage.

The curse of finishing second passed down to his son who had already turned professional by the time his father claimed the last of those near misses in 2010.

Evans clinched his first WRC stage win in Germany in 2014 and a first podium in Argentina a year later, before having to drop down to the WRC2 class in 2016.

Evans admitted that blow only fueled his determination to make it in the WRC and a first rally victory followed - in his home event in Wales - in 2017.

He has been remarkably consistent, finishing second for the title in 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024 and, perhaps most agonisingly, to Sebastien Ogier by just four points in the final race of 2025.

He appeared condemned to be one of sport's great runners-up until the late drama of Sardinia threw up one of the championship's most thrilling finishes.

There may have been a stroke of fortune about the title win, but few can deny Evans earned it.

articles.title: Panthers HC Dave Canales’ admission makes Tetairoa McMillan’s SNF start more impressive
articles.summary: Dave Canales was honest about Tetairoa McMillan’s form heading into Week 4 before the star receiver dominated in the Carolina Panthers’ 32-26 win over the De...
articles.body:
Dave Canales was honest about Tetairoa McMillan 's form heading into Week 4 before the star receiver dominated in the Carolina Panthers' 32-26 win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday night.

McMillan is going through the second season of his budding NFL career with the Panthers. Following a promising rookie year, he looks to build on that early success and firmly cement himself as an elite receiver among the best the league has to offer.

McMillan certainly showed out with explosive plays throughout Carolina's primetime clash with Detroit. He made 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, setting records in the process. Canales reflected on the receiver's efforts after the game, revealing details about him and Bryce Young during practices ahead of the game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I got to be honest. It was not a great week of practice for the two of them. There were some misses. They had to work through some stuff and talk through it. I've been a part of this before, where you don't make the judgement on what's going to happen on Sunday as the guys continue to work and find that. Then for it to show up like that was beautiful," Canales said, via reporter Joe Person.

How Tetairoa McMillan, Panthers played against Lions

Tetairoa McMillan amazed fans with his performance, helping Dave Canales and the Panthers fend off the Lions.

Both teams traded blows throughout the first half, being even at 16 apiece. Carolina took control and didn't look back in the last 30 minutes of regulation, outscoring Detroit 16-10 in that stretch.

Bryce Young enjoyed a great night leading the attack. He completed 29 out of 41 passes for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Chuba Hubbard flourished in the run game, racking up 20 carries for 122 yards and two touchdowns.

The Panthers will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They are on bye next week before resuming action against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6 as kickoff commences on Oct. 18 at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries relieved to end losing streak in major finals after comeback win over Gerwyn Price
articles.summary: Luke Humphries produced one of the greatest fightbacks in World Grand Prix history to defeat Gerwyn Price 6-4 in the final; Humphries won the double-start event for a second time and extended Price's wait too claim another ranked TV title
articles.body:
Humphries reached a record-breaking fourth consecutive final at the double-start tournament, where he battled back from 3-0 down to win six of the next seven sets in an impressive 6-4 win over the Welshman.

Victory at Leicester's Mattioli Arena followed his win over Price in the 2023 final and makes him just the fourth player ever to claim multiple World Grand Prix titles, with Humphries' latest success securing him the £150,000 first prize.

Humphries' victory is his first ranked TV major title since the Winmau World Masters in February 2025, with 'Cool Hand' pleased for his streak of runner-up finishes to end.

"I'm just happy to get one back," said Humphries, who was second at the World Grand Prix, European Championship and Grand Slam of Darts last year before starting 2026 with runner-up finishes at the Winmau World Masters and Premier League.

"It's nice to have that run of losses in major finals off my back. It feels really special - this really means the world to me.

"I needed this to give me a bit of confidence. It's been a torrid 15 or 18 months for myself losing so many major finals."

Humphries needed to take out a 105 finish in a final-leg decider to avoid going 4-0 down against Price, who missed set darts to move 5-4 up before losing a topsy-turvy contest.

"I worked incredibly hard from 3-0 down there, showed a lot of grit and determination," Humphries added. "These wins are more sweet than the ones you win with ease.

"I felt like I had not much to give tonight [Sunday]. I just didn't want to lose 6-0 and I wanted to give the fans something to be happy with, and all of a sudden I find myself 4-3 up.

"I'm looking forward to taking the trophy home to my son, who can finally see his dad have another trophy and it not be a runners-up one!"

Humphries back Price to end major drought 'soon'

Price remains without a major title since 2022 after a third consecutive runner-up finish, having also finished second at the World Matchplay to Luke Littler and at the World Series Finals to Ross Smith, with the Ice Man also having three other semi-final appearances in majors this year.

"Gezzy was amazing for those first three sets, absolutely insane," Humphries insisted. "He is going to win a major title soon. It's written in the stars for him, he can't keep playing this well and not win."

Price opened with a 132.62 average in the opening set, which he completed in just 34 darts to post the best three-dart set average in tournament history, although now has three runner-up finishes at the World Grand Prix since his 2020 success.

"I don't want to win a major, do I?!" Price told Sky Sports. "It's gutting I lost another one - I'm not bothered, but I am bothered.

"Luke played brilliantly in the middle part of the game, but I still squandered so many opportunities to put him under a bit of pressure. I felt like it was a fantastic game - I thought I played brilliantly, and Luke played brilliantly."

Mardle: Humphries didn't succumb under pressure

"Humphries was in trouble, then a bit more and then a bit more - so to get out of it was an incredible effort. The last two sets were his best. He was under the cosh for more than an hour but didn't succumb. He stood up to everything Gezzy [Price] threw at him, which was a lot!

"When you have won before, which Luke has done many times and in many, ways, there is that belief of, 'I'm under pressure, but let's just see as I know my game can win', rather than 'oh no, I am going to get beat'. He played his game and he won.

"Gezzy tightened up after a great start. He says things in the spur of the moment but the way he competes, he wants it. You can't play like he did this evening if you don't care!

"It is disheartening and disappointing when you are 3-0 up and don't win, but he has lost enough finals to know nothing is a given. He is still a young man and will get many more opportunities. He knows he is good enough."
